items.name: The LORD describes the wild ass's pasture

pat_dated_flood_notice.name: Dated notice of the waters' state
pat_dated_flood_notice.desc: Repeated shape "in the [n]th month, on the [n]th day of the month" attached to a stage of the drying: v.4-5 and v.13-14.

items.label: occurs as
items.name: God remembers Noah and the waters go down

pat_esau_is_edom.name: Closing Identification "Esau is Edom"
pat_esau_is_edom.desc: Recurring closing tag: "Esau, he is Edom" (v8), "the sons of Esau, he is Edom" (v19), "he is Esau, the father of Edom" (v43).

items.label: occurs as
items.name: the chiefs of Edom by Their Places

pat_these_are_heading.name: "These are..." List Heading
pat_these_are_heading.desc: Each unit opens with a naming formula: "these are the generations of Esau", "These are the chiefs of the sons of Esau", "These are the sons of Seir", "these are the kings who reigned", "these are the names of the chiefs".

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Esau's Wives and Sons in Canaan

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The Sons and Chiefs of Seir the Horite

items.label: occurs as
items.name: the chiefs of Edom by Their Places

patara.name: Patara
patara.desc: Port where Paul changed ships for Phoenicia.

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: the voice crying in the wilderness at Mark 1:3

paths.name: paths
paths.desc: The ways Job walks, from 'stand watch over all my paths'.

patience.name: patience
patience.desc: **The hinge in both endurance chains** -- 'suffering produces perseverance' (Rom 5:3) and 'the testing of your faith develops perseverance' (Jas 1:3). It is what suffering is said to produce, and in both places it is a stage and not the end.

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: hope that is seen is no hope at all

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: Older men are to be temperate, dignified, self-controlled

patmos.name: Patmos
patmos.desc: Island where John received the Revelation.

pattern_address_to_friends.name: Second-Person Reproach of the Friends
pattern_address_to_friends.desc: "you" address recurs at the speech's opening, middle and close: "How long will you torment my soul", "you, my friends", "Be afraid for yourselves of the sword"

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Warning of Judgment on the Friends

pattern_altar_called_on_name.name: Abram builds an altar to the LORD
pattern_altar_called_on_name.desc: "the place of the altar that he had made there at the first, and there Abram called on the name of the LORD" and "built there an altar to the LORD" frame the chapter.

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Abram settles at Mamre and builds an altar

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Abram returns from Egypt to Bethel

pattern_and_god_said_unto_abraham.name: "And God said to Abraham" opens each new demand
pattern_and_god_said_unto_abraham.desc: v.9 "And God said to Abraham, And you shall keep my covenant"; v.15 "And God said to Abraham, As for Sarai your wife" — the repeated formula marks each internal seam of the speech.

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Sarah renamed, Isaac promised, Abraham laughs

pattern_and_it_came_to_pass.name: And it came to pass (scene hinge)
pattern_and_it_came_to_pass.desc: "And it happened, when Jacob saw Rachel" (v10), "when Laban heard the news" (v13), "in the evening" (v23), "in the morning, behold, she was Leah" (v25) mark turns inside scenes rather than between them

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Jacob at the Well and Welcome by Laban

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Judah marries a Canaanite and has three sons

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Tamar accused, and Judah acknowledges the pledge

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The birth of Perez and Zerah

items.label: occurs as
items.name: She seizes his garment and he flees

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Her accusation to the household and to her husband

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The master's wife propositions Joseph and he refuses

pattern_answered_and_said.name: X answered and said (speech opening)
pattern_answered_and_said.desc: "And the LORD answered Job and said"; "And Job answered the LORD and said"; "And the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said"

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The LORD's challenge to the one who contends

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The LORD's second speech from the whirlwind

pattern_appearance_unbelief.name: Jesus appears; hearers do not believe
pattern_appearance_unbelief.desc: each reports 'he appeared' followed by a report to others and 'believed not'

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Appearance to two on the road

pattern_as_god_commanded.name: As God commanded him
pattern_as_god_commanded.desc: Repeated obedience formula: "according to all that the LORD commanded him" (v5), "as God commanded Noah" (v9), "as God commanded him" (v16).

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The Day the Deep Broke Up

items.label: occurs as
items.name: God's Last Command to Enter the Ark

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Noah and the Creatures Go In

pattern_back_from_pit.name: Kept Back from the Pit
pattern_back_from_pit.desc: "He holds back his soul from the pit" (v.18), "Redeem him from going down to the pit" (v.24), "from passing into the pit" (v.28), "to bring back his soul from the pit" (v.30).

items.label: occurs as
items.name: God Speaks in Dreams to Turn Man Back

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Chastening by Sickness and Rescue by the Ransom

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Summary: God Works Thus with Man

pattern_behold_appeal.name: "Behold" opening an appeal to shared knowledge
pattern_behold_appeal.desc: "Behold, you have instructed many" (v.3) and "Behold, he does not trust his servants" (v.18) each introduce evidence for the argument

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The voice: no man is pure before God

items.label: occurs as
items.name: You instructed others, now you faint

pattern_behold_marker.name: "Behold" Opening a Turn
pattern_behold_marker.desc: Repeated "Behold" at vv. 2, 6, 7, 12 marks each new step of the argument.

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Elihu Quotes Job's Complaint and Answers

pattern_beyond_comprehension.name: He is past finding out
pattern_beyond_comprehension.desc: Twice a section closes on the limit of human knowledge: "he does great things and we do not know" (v.5) and "The Almighty, we have not found him" (v.23).

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The Voice of God in the Thunder

pattern_blessing_of_abraham.name: Blessing formula: be fruitful, multiply, inherit the land
pattern_blessing_of_abraham.desc: Isaac: "make you fruitful, and multiply you... that you may possess the land"; the LORD: "your seed will be like the dust of the earth... to you I will give it, and to your seed".

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Isaac's Charge and Blessing to Jacob

pattern_border_and_dwelling.name: Territory note closing a branch
pattern_border_and_dwelling.desc: "And the border of the Canaanite was from Sidon, as you come toward Gerar" (v.19) matches "And their dwelling was from Mesha, as you come toward Sephar" (v.30) -- same shape, geographic limits given just before the colophon.

pattern_bow_and_speak.name: Abraham bows, then speaks a new proposal
pattern_bow_and_speak.desc: 'And Abraham rose and bowed down to the people of the land' (v7) and 'And Abraham bowed down before the people of the land' (v12) each open a fresh round of negotiation.

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The price agreed and the silver weighed

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Abraham names Ephron's cave; Ephron offers it

pattern_bowed_worshipped.name: He bowed down and worshiped the LORD
pattern_bowed_worshipped.desc: Repeated act at each confirmation: "And the man bowed his head and worshiped the LORD" (v.26); "he worshiped the LORD, bowing himself to the ground" (v.52); also recounted in v.48

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Her family named; the servant blesses the LORD

pattern_brother_speaks_up.name: A brother interposes: "Let us not"
pattern_brother_speaks_up.desc: Twice a named brother breaks the plot with a proposal: "And Reuben heard it... Let us not kill him" and "And Judah said... let us sell him."

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Judah's plan: sold to the traders

pattern_came_to_pass.name: And it happened, when...
pattern_came_to_pass.desc: Both scene-openings use the same temporal formula: "And it happened, when he drew near to enter Egypt" and "And it happened, when Abram came into Egypt".

pattern_can_you_question.name: Rhetorical 'Have/Can you...?' Challenge
pattern_can_you_question.desc: Each unit opens with a second-person challenge — "Have you commanded the morning", "Have you entered the springs of the sea", "Have you entered the storehouses of snow", "Can you bind", "Can you lift up your voice", "Will you hunt the prey".

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The Deep, Death, and the Dwelling of Light

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Clouds and Lightning at Your Command

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Who Feeds the Lion and the Raven

pattern_creature_challenge.name: Do You Know / Can You Do This? — Challenge Opening a Creature Portrait
pattern_creature_challenge.desc: Each unit opens with a second-person interrogative addressed to Job — 'Do you know', 'Who sent out', 'Will the wild ox... serve you', 'Did you give', 'Do you give', 'Does the hawk soar by your understanding' — then drops the question and describes the creature in the third person.

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The Wild Goats and the Hinds Giving Birth

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The Wild Ox Will Not Serve You

pattern_death_and_burial.name: Death and burial notice with a named place
pattern_death_and_burial.desc: 'died, and she was buried below Bethel'; 'Rachel died, and was buried on the road to Ephrath'; 'died, and was gathered to his people... his sons... buried him'.

items.label: occurs as
items.name: God sends Jacob to Bethel; the strange gods buried

pattern_dew_fatness.name: "The dew of heaven and the richness of the earth"
pattern_dew_fatness.desc: Both oracles use the same pair: "the dew of the heavens, and the fatness of the earth" (v.28) and "the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of the heavens" (v.39).

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Jacob Deceives Isaac and Receives the Blessing

pattern_embalming_death_notice.name: Death, embalming, and burial notice
pattern_embalming_death_notice.desc: Both frame the chapter with the same acts: 'the physicians embalmed Israel' and 'they embalmed him, and he was placed in a coffin in Egypt.'

pattern_evil_beast_devoured.name: "An evil beast has devoured him"
pattern_evil_beast_devoured.desc: The lie is planned in v20, "we will say, An evil beast has devoured him", and spoken by Jacob in v33, "an evil beast has devoured him."

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The bloodied coat and Jacob's mourning

pattern_famine_exchange.name: Petition to Joseph answered by an exchange
pattern_famine_exchange.desc: Twice the people come and speak ('Give us bread, and why should we die before you?' / 'buy us and our land for bread'), and Joseph takes a new possession in return.

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Bread bought with money, then cattle

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The second year: land and persons sold

pattern_fate_of_the_wicked.name: The lamp of the wicked put out
pattern_fate_of_the_wicked.desc: Repeated third-person future declarations of doom: "the light of the wicked will go out", "his lamp above him will go out", "They will thrust him from light into darkness"

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Destruction, extinction of name and seed

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The wicked man's light put out and snares laid

pattern_fell_on_his_face.name: Abraham falls on his face before God's word
pattern_fell_on_his_face.desc: v.3 "And Abram fell on his face"; v.17 "And Abraham fell on his face and laughed" — the same gesture, once in awe, once in disbelief.

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Sarah renamed, Isaac promised, Abraham laughs

pattern_find_grace.name: Seeking Grace in My Lord's Sight
pattern_find_grace.desc: "These are to find favor in the eyes of my lord" (v.8) and "let me find favor in the eyes of my lord" (v.15); cf. "if now I have found favor in your eyes" (v.10)

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The Family Presented and the Gift Pressed

pattern_go_to_let_us.name: 'Go to, let us...' resolve
pattern_go_to_let_us.desc: 'Come, let us make bricks' and 'Come, let us build ourselves a city' are answered by 'Come, let us go down, and there confuse their language'.

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The LORD comes down and scatters them

pattern_god_forbid.name: "God forbid" refusal
pattern_god_forbid.desc: Brothers: "Far be it from your servants to do such a thing"; Joseph: "Far be it from me to do this".

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Before Joseph: Judah's first plea and Joseph's sentence

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The search and the cup found in Benjamin's sack

pattern_god_saw_corrupt_earth.name: God saw the earth and it was corrupt
pattern_god_saw_corrupt_earth.desc: Twice the divine inspection precedes the sentence: "And the LORD saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth" (v.5) and "And God looked upon the earth and saw that it was corrupt" (v.12), each leading to the announcement "I will destroy".

items.label: occurs as
items.name: God Resolves to Destroy Man, but Noah Finds Grace

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The Generations of Noah and the Corrupt Earth

pattern_god_shews_pharaoh.name: God has shown Pharaoh what He is about to do
pattern_god_shews_pharaoh.desc: Repeated in the interpretation: "God has told Pharaoh what He is about to do" (v25) and "What God is about to do He has shown to Pharaoh" (v28); echoed by Pharaoh, "Since God has made known to you all this".

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Joseph interprets: seven plenty, seven famine

pattern_gray_hairs_grave.name: bring my gray hair down to Sheol in sorrow
pattern_gray_hairs_grave.desc: Repeated in v29 "you will bring down my gray hair in calamity to Sheol" and v31 "will bring down the gray hair of your servant our father in sorrow to Sheol".

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Judah recounts the father and the youngest son

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Judah offers himself in Benjamin's place

pattern_hated_him_yet_the_more.name: they hated him even more
pattern_hated_him_yet_the_more.desc: The escalating refrain of the brothers' feeling: "they hated him" (v4), "they hated him even more" (v5), "they hated him even more for his dreams" (v8), "his brothers were jealous of him" (v11).

pattern_he_blessed.name: "And he blessed..." blessing formula
pattern_he_blessed.desc: "And he blessed Joseph, and said" (v15) and "And he blessed them that day, saying" (v20) each introduce a blessing.

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The crossed hands and the blessing of the lads

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Joseph objects; Jacob prefers the younger

pattern_he_has_afflicted_me.name: "He has..." Chain of Divine Assault
pattern_he_has_afflicted_me.desc: repeated third-person clauses with God as subject: "He has walled up my way", "He has stripped my glory from me", "He has torn me down on every side", "He has kindled His anger", "He has put my brothers far from me"

pattern_hear_me_my_lord.name: 'My lord, hear me' opening of each reply
pattern_hear_me_my_lord.desc: 'Listen to us, sir' (v6), 'No, my lord. Listen to me' (v11), 'Listen to me, my lord' (v15) — a courtesy formula marking each speech.

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The price agreed and the silver weighed

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Abraham asks the sons of Heth for a burial place

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Abraham names Ephron's cave; Ephron offers it

pattern_hear_my_speech.name: Summons to listen before a plea
pattern_hear_my_speech.desc: "Hear now my argument, and listen to the pleadings of my lips" (v6) and "Listen carefully to my speech, and my declaration in your ears" (v17) each open a new appeal

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Let me alone, I will plead my own cause

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Warning to the friends who plead God's case

pattern_hearken_summons.name: Summons to Hear Me
pattern_hearken_summons.desc: "hear my speeches, and give ear to all my words" (v.1) and "hear me: be silent" (vv.31,33) frame the speech with the same call.

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Renewed Summons to Silence and Instruction

pattern_here_am_i.name: Called by name, answering "Here am I"
pattern_here_am_i.desc: "said to him, Abraham: and he said, Here I am" (v.1) and "Abraham, Abraham: and he said, Here I am" (v.11); Isaac's call to his father echoes it in v.7.

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The angel stays his hand; the ram and Jehovah-jireh

items.label: occurs as
items.name: God commands the sacrifice of Isaac

pattern_i_will_make_a_nation.name: Promise to make Ishmael a nation
pattern_i_will_make_a_nation.desc: "of the son of the slave woman I will make him into a nation" (v13) and "for I will make him into a great nation" (v18).

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Hagar and Ishmael in the wilderness

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Sarah demands Hagar be cast out

pattern_if_i_then.name: "If I ... yet/then" hypothetical of futile self-defence
pattern_if_i_then.desc: "If it is a matter of strength", "If I am righteous", "If I say, I will forget my complaint", "If I wash myself with snow; then You will plunge me"

items.label: occurs as
items.name: I would not dare answer him

items.label: occurs as
items.name: My days flee and I cannot comfort myself

pattern_israel_said_unto_joseph.name: "And Israel/Jacob said to Joseph" speech-opener
pattern_israel_said_unto_joseph.desc: Each new speech to Joseph is marked by the same formula: "And Jacob said unto Joseph" (v3), "And Israel said unto Joseph" (v11, v21).

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Jacob's parting word and the extra portion to Joseph

pattern_knew_bare.name: He knew his wife; she conceived and gave birth
pattern_knew_bare.desc: Repeated begetting formula: "And Adam had relations with his wife Eve, and she conceived and gave birth to Cain" / "And Cain had relations with his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Enoch" / "And Adam again had relations with his wife, and she gave birth to a son".

pattern_let_us_make_our_father_drink_win.name: let us get our father drunk with wine

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Come, let us get our father drunk with wine

items.label: occurs as
items.name: I slept with my father last night

pattern_lift_up_eyes_and_see.name: Lifting up the eyes and beholding land
pattern_lift_up_eyes_and_see.desc: "And Lot lifted up his eyes, and saw all the plain of the Jordan" is answered by "Lift up now your eyes, and see... northward, and southward" -- same gesture, one man's choosing, one God's giving.

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Lot chooses the plain of Jordan

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The LORD promises the land and the seed

pattern_lived_fathered_died.name: X lived N years and fathered Y... and all his days were N: and he died
pattern_lived_fathered_died.desc: Ten repetitions of a fixed three-verse shape: age at fathering, remaining years with 'and had other sons and daughters', then 'So X lived a total of ... years, and then he died.' Enoch and Noah are the marked exceptions.

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Lamech and the naming of Noah

pattern_lord_god_formed.name: "And the Lord God" + act of forming or planting
pattern_lord_god_formed.desc: Each new movement opens with the divine name and a verb of making: "the LORD God formed the man", "the LORD God planted a garden", "the LORD God took the man", "from the ground the LORD God formed every beast", "the LORD God caused a deep sleep".

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The man set in the garden and commanded

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The search for a help meet and the making of woman

items.label: occurs as
items.name: A second beginning: the man formed of dust

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The garden in Eden and its rivers

pattern_lord_said_unto_cain.name: And the LORD said to Cain
pattern_lord_said_unto_cain.desc: Each divine turn is opened by "And the LORD said to Cain" / "And the LORD said to him".

pattern_lord_with_joseph_prosper.name: The LORD was with Joseph, and he prospered under a master's hand
pattern_lord_with_joseph_prosper.desc: "And the LORD was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man" / "But the LORD was with Joseph, and extended kindness to him"; both end with all things committed to Joseph's hand and the master looking to nothing.

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The LORD with Joseph in prison

pattern_made_sure.name: 'Made sure to Abraham for a possession'
pattern_made_sure.desc: Repeated conveyance formula at v17-18 and v20 frames the burial notice.

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The field made sure to Abraham

pattern_mischief_befall_him.name: Jacob's fear that mischief will befall Benjamin
pattern_mischief_befall_him.desc: "Lest harm befall him" (v4) and "if harm befalls him on the way" (v38) frame the chapter

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Jacob Sends His Sons to Egypt for Corn

pattern_naming_a_son.name: Mother speaks and names the son
pattern_naming_a_son.desc: Repeated shape: birth, then "And [Rachel/Leah] said, [explanation]... and she called his name [X]" -- Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Issachar, Zebulun, Joseph.

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The mandrakes and Leah's later children

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Rachel gives Bilhah to Jacob; Dan and Naphtali

items.label: occurs as
items.name: God remembers Rachel: the birth of Joseph

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Leah gives Zilpah to Jacob; Gad and Asher

pattern_naming_etymology.name: A name is given and explained
pattern_naming_etymology.desc: "Abraham called the name of his son... Isaac" answered by Sarah's "God has made laughter for me"; and "Therefore he called that place Beersheba; because there the two of them swore."

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Abraham's covenant with Abimelech at Beersheba

pattern_naming_the_child.name: Conception, birth, and naming
pattern_naming_the_child.desc: "And she conceived, and bore a son; and he called his name Er" repeats through the sons, and recurs at the twins: "his name was called Perez", "his name was called Zerah".

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Judah marries a Canaanite and has three sons

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The birth of Perez and Zerah

pattern_nature_contrast.name: Nature's Image Turned Against Man
pattern_nature_contrast.desc: Twice a figure from nature is drawn out and then applied to man's end: "For there is hope for a tree... But a man dies"; "The waters wear away the stones... You destroy the hope of man".

items.label: occurs as
items.name: You Destroy the Hope of Man

items.label: occurs as
items.name: A Tree Sprouts Again, But Man Does Not

pattern_obey_my_voice.name: "Now therefore... obey my voice"
pattern_obey_my_voice.desc: Rebekah's command formula recurs: "Now, my son, listen to my voice according to what I command you" (v.8) and "Now, my son, listen to my voice; and arise, flee" (v.43).

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Esau's Grudge and Rebekah Sends Jacob Away

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: Show yourself a pattern of good works

pattern_oh_that_wish.name: "Oh that" wish
pattern_oh_that_wish.desc: "If only my grief were fully weighed" (v.2) and "Oh that my request might come" (v.8) each open a unit with the same optative formula.

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Wish for death, and no strength left

pattern_peradventure_bargain.name: Suppose there are N righteous / for the sake of N I will not do it
pattern_peradventure_bargain.desc: Repeated exchange shape: "Perhaps there are fifty righteous" / "If I find in Sodom fifty righteous... I will spare"; "Perhaps forty will be found there" / "I will not do it for the sake of the forty"; through "Perhaps ten will be found there" / "I will not destroy it for the sake of the ten."

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The Descending Numbers: Forty-Five to Ten

pattern_peradventure_x_found_there_i_wil.name: Perhaps there be X found there; I will not destroy it

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The LORD: on account of the forty, I will not do it

pattern_perfect_upright.name: Perfect and Upright, Feared God, Shunned Evil
pattern_perfect_upright.desc: The same fourfold description of Job appears in the narrator's opening (v. 1) and in the LORD's speech to Satan (v. 8): "a blameless and upright man, fearing God and turning away from evil".

items.label: occurs as
items.name: The LORD and Satan in the Heavenly Court

pattern_pharisee_objection.name: Pharisees/scribes object, Jesus answers
pattern_pharisee_objection.desc: each unit follows the shape: an authority figure questions or objects to Jesus' conduct ('Why does this man...', 'Why does He eat...', 'Why don’t Your disciples...', 'why are they doing what is unlawful...'), and Jesus responds with a saying or parable

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Calling Levi and eating with sinners

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Question about fasting and the bridegroom/cloth/wine sayings

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Scribes' objection and the healing proof

pattern_pillar_set_up.name: Jacob sets up a pillar to mark a place
pattern_pillar_set_up.desc: 'And Jacob set up a pillar in the place where he spoke with him' / 'And Jacob set up a pillar over her grave'.

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Renaming at Bethel and the promise

pattern_place_naming.name: he named that place
pattern_place_naming.desc: "he called the name of that place Mahanaim" and "Jacob called the name of the place Peniel" -- each encounter with God closes in a naming

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Wrestling at the Jabbok; Jacob named Israel

pattern_quoting_job.name: For you said — quoting Job back at him
pattern_quoting_job.desc: Elihu builds each turn on a cited saying: "you said, My righteousness is more than God's", "For you say, What advantage", "How much less when you say you do not see him".

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Trust him, Job speaks in vain

pattern_relay_command.name: Say to him: relayed message
pattern_relay_command.desc: Both Joseph and Pharaoh issue messages to be carried: "say to him, Thus says your son Joseph" and "Say to your brothers, Do this"

items.label: occurs as
items.name: Joseph's speech: God sent me before you

pattern_rhetorical_can_you.name: "Can you / Who can" unanswerable question
pattern_rhetorical_can_you.desc: "Can you draw out Leviathan", "Can you fill his skin", then "Who can uncover the face of his garment?", "Who can open the doors of his face?" — the same interrogative form asserting human incapacity.

items.label: occurs as

pattern_rhetorical_question_pair.name: Paired rhetorical questions from nature and body

plagues_of_egypt.name: the plagues of Egypt
plagues_of_egypt.desc:
Ten in Exodus 7 to 12: the river turned to blood, frogs, lice, flies, a severe plague on the livestock, boils, hail, locusts, darkness, and the death of the firstborn.

The text's own word for them is signs rather than punishments — 'I will multiply My signs and wonders in the land of Egypt' (Exod 7:3) — and it says what they are for: 'that you may tell your children and grandchildren how severely I dealt with the Egyptians' (10:2). They are given as something to be recounted afterwards.

The word plague appears too, and later: 'I will send all My plagues against you' (9:14), and 'I will bring yet one more plague' (11:1).

Two psalms retell them and neither keeps the order or the count. Psalm 78:44-51 gives seven and Psalm 105:28-36 gives eight, in different sequences.

power.name: power
power.desc:
'But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you' (Acts 1:8).

Two hundred and sixty verses use the word, and in the letters it is almost always attached to something rather than held: the power of God (Rom 1:16), the power of the cross (1Cor 1:18), the power of Christ (2Cor 12:9), the power of his might (Eph 6:10). Where it is given to people it is given (Acts 1:8) rather than possessed.

Rom 8:38 lists 'powers' among the things that cannot separate, which is the same word doing a different job -- there it names something opposed rather than something received.

'On that day David first committed to Asaph and his associates this song of thanksgiving to the LORD:' (1Chr 16:7), running from 16:8 to 16:36.

**It is assembled out of three psalms that also stand on their own.** 16:8-22 is Psalm 105:1-15, 16:23-33 is Psalm 96, and 16:34-36 is Psalm 106:1 with 106:47-48. Chronicles gives the composite one occasion and one deliverer; the psalter carries the pieces separately and unattributed to this day.

That makes it a harder case than an ordinary parallel passage: not one text told twice, but **one text quoting three others, none of which it names**.

renewal.name: renewal
renewal.desc:
'be transformed by the renewing of your mind' (Rom 12:2).

A thread that runs the length of the text and is never once cross-referenced. Renew a right spirit (Ps 51:10); a new heart and a new spirit (Ezek 36:26); renew their strength (Isa 40:31); the renewing of your mind (Rom 12:2); to be renewed in the spirit of your minds (Eph 4:23); renewed in knowledge (Col 3:10); the renewing of the Holy Spirit (Titus 3:5); the inward man renewed day by day (2Cor 4:16).

Eight passages, five writers, both testaments, and what is renewed is different every time — spirit, heart, strength, mind, knowledge, the inward man. The passages join because they share a word, and say no more than that.

resurrection_of_christ.name: the resurrection of Christ
resurrection_of_christ.desc:
'Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.' (1Cor 15:20).

The empty tomb is told as narrative—who ran where, who saw whom—but the letters use the resurrection as the ground of their argument.

1 Corinthians 15 stakes everything on it and says so twice, in the negative: 'And if Christ has not been raised, our preaching is worthless, and so is your faith' (15:14), and 'And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile; you are still in your sins' (15:17). The chapter argues by supposing the opposite.

Romans splits the work between the two events: 'delivered over to death for our trespasses and was raised to life for our justification' (4:25). Two clauses, two purposes.

The vocabulary is worth watching. Fifty-four verses say risen or rose again, forty-two say raised him or raised up, forty say resurrection—and the passive is the commoner form: he is more often raised than rises.

'Now there was a rich man dressed in purple and fine linen' (Luke 16:19), and Lazarus at his gate; both die, and the conversation that follows is held across a gulf between Abraham and the rich man.

The text does not call it a parable — Luke 15:3 says 'Then Jesus told them this parable' of the lost sheep, and no such marker introduces this one. It is filed as a parable here on its form, which is a reading; that it names one of its characters is unique among them.

Luke 16 opens 'Jesus also said to His disciples' (16:1), after 'Then Jesus told them this parable' (15:3).

Whether that reckoning is a change in standing or in the person is among the oldest disputes about these texts, and the verses settle nothing.

**It is in almost every scene that matters**: before Pharaoh (7:10), stretched over the sea (14:16), held up over the battle with Amalek (17:9), and struck against the rock at Meribah when he was told to speak (Num 20:11).

She denies it and the text records the denial and the contradiction in one verse: 'But Sarah was afraid, so she denied it and said, I did not laugh. No, replied the LORD, but you did laugh' (18:15).

The laughing comes back as the child's name and as her own reading of it: 'God has made me laugh, and everyone who hears of this will laugh with me' (21:6). Abraham had laughed first, at 17:17, and nobody reproves him for it.

sermon_on_the_mount.name: the Sermon on the Mount
sermon_on_the_mount.desc:
'When Jesus saw the crowds, He went up on the mountain and sat down. His disciples came to Him, and He began to teach them, saying' (Matt 5:1-2), closing at 7:28 with 'the crowds were astonished at His teaching'.

Its imagery works by assertion and depiction rather than comparison. 'You are the salt of the earth' carries no marker; the two houses are a scene set down beside its point. Two templates run through it: the beatitude, 'Blessed are X, for Y', eight times in 5:3-10 with the ground stated each time; and the antithesis, 'You have heard that it was said ... But I tell you', six times in 5:21-44, each quoting a commandment without naming it.

servant_of_abraham.desc:

He swears the oath, travels to the city of Nahor, sets the test at the well and brings Rebekah back — forty-five verses of a chapter of sixty-seven, and the text never gives him a name.

He is commonly identified with Eliezer of Damascus (Gen 15:2), and that reading may well be right. Genesis 24 does not make it.

seventy_elders_of_israel.name: the seventy elders

'Bring Me seventy of the elders of Israel known to you as leaders and officers of the people' (Num 11:16), appointed to carry the burden Moses says he cannot carry alone.

The only passage where the Spirit is described as divided: 'I will take some of the Spirit that is on you and put that Spirit on them' (11:17), and 'As the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied — but they never did so again' (11:25).

Two of the seventy, Eldad and Medad, are not at the tabernacle and prophesy in the camp anyway. Joshua asks Moses to stop them and is answered: 'I wish that all the LORD’s people were prophets and that the LORD would place His Spirit on them' (11:29).

son_of_man.name: the son of man
son_of_man.desc:
A human being, mortal and small before God: 'what is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You care for him?' (Ps 8:4; also Job 25:6, Isa 51:12). Num 23:19 sets 'a son of man' against God: 'God is not a man, that He should lie, or a son of man, that He should change His mind.'

In Ezekiel it is how the prophet is addressed, 93 times in the Berean -- 'Son of man,' He said to me, 'stand up on your feet' (Ezek 2:1) -- and Daniel is addressed so once (Dan 8:17). Daniel also sees one 'like a son of man' coming with the clouds of heaven (Dan 7:13; the Berean's 'the Son of Man', article and capitals, is a translators' choice -- the Aramaic reads 'like a son of man'). The title Jesus uses in the Gospels has its own card, the Son of Man.

son_of_shelomith.name: the son of Shelomith
son_of_shelomith.desc:
'Now the son of an Israelite mother and an Egyptian father went out among the Israelites ... The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name with a curse' (Lev 24:10-11).

His mother is named and he is not: 'His mother’s name was Shelomith daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan' (24:11). That is the reverse of the text's usual habit, and it is why this passage is recorded — a man known only as somebody's son, in a book that names his mother, her father and her tribe.

song_of_david_at_deliverance.name: David's song of deliverance
song_of_david_at_deliverance.desc:
'And David sang this song to the LORD on the day the LORD had delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.' (2Sam 22:1).

The text carries it twice, as 2 Samuel 22 and Psalm 18, with the superscription of the psalm giving the same occasion in almost the same words. The two run parallel for fifty verses and differ constantly in small things — 2Sam 22:3 has 'my shield, and the horn of my salvation. My stronghold, my refuge', Ps 18:2 'my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my stronghold'.

Its opening verses stack more figures for God than any other passage of comparable length: rock, fortress, deliverer, shield, horn of salvation, high tower, refuge, saviour, in two verses.

song_of_moses.name: the song of Moses
song_of_moses.desc:
'Now therefore, write down for yourselves this song and teach it to the Israelites; have them recite it, so that it may be a witness for Me against them.' (Deut 31:19), and it runs through Deuteronomy 32.

Given as a witness against them, and taught to them so they will carry it themselves. The reasoning is stated at 31:21: it will not be forgotten from the lips of their descendants.

Revelation 15:3 names 'the song of God’s servant Moses and of the Lamb' together, which is Scripture reaching back for this by name.

spoken_in_proverbs.name: I have spoken to you in proverbs
spoken_in_proverbs.desc:
'I have spoken these things to you in figures of speech. An hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you this way, but will tell you plainly about the Father.' (John 16:25).

The text naming its own manner of speech. It marks the figures as figures, and promises plainness later — and the disciples answer at 16:29, 'See, now You are speaking plainly and without figures of speech'.

Translations differ on the word: 'dark sayings' and 'proverbs' point opposite ways. A proverb is pithy and meant to be caught; a dark saying is meant to be worked at.

stand_on_holy_ground.name: the place where you are standing is holy
stand_on_holy_ground.desc:
'Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground' (Exod 3:5).

Said twice in the text and quoted a third time. Joshua gets almost the same sentence from The Commander of the LORD’s army at Jericho: 'Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy.' (Josh 5:15). Stephen quotes the Exodus version back at the council (Acts 7:33).

The two scenes are built alike — a man alone, a figure that is not a man, an instruction about footwear before anything else is said — and the text draws no connection between them. Joshua is Moses's successor and this is the nearest the book comes to saying so without saying it.

A phrase search for 'holy ground' finds Exodus and Acts and misses Joshua, which says only 'is holy'. Noted here because the near miss is exactly the kind a reader makes and an index does not.

Does it tie to the tabernacle? Not in the text. The text has a great deal of holiness-of-place language — the holy place, the most holy, the sanctuary, most of it in Ezekiel, Leviticus, Numbers and Exodus — and Psalm 15:1 even sets tabernacle and holy hill in parallel. But nothing joins any of it to the ground at the bush. The phrase 'holy ground' is these two verses and no more.

The gesture does not carry the meaning either. Removing a shoe recurs four more times for reasons that have nothing to do with holiness: a legal repudiation before the elders (Deut 25:9), a sign of coming captivity (Isa 20:2-4), and David going barefoot up the Mount of Olives in mourning (2Sam 15:30).

So the connection a reader feels between this ground and the sanctuary is a reader's, and a good one, and not the text's.

'Now look to the heavens and count the stars, if you are able.” Then He told him, “So shall your offspring be.' (Gen 15:5).

**The next verse is the one the whole argument about faith and works runs on**: 'Abram believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness' (15:6). Paul cites it at Romans 4:3 and James at 2:23, each in his own argument.

Genesis 22:17 repeats the figure and adds a second: 'like the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore'.

temple.name: The Temple
temple.desc:
The house built for the LORD in Jerusalem. The temple as a figure has its own card: [[image_temple]].

**Solomon built the first:** 'The house that King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high' (1 Kings 6:2). At its dedication 'the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD' (1 Kings 8:11), and Solomon prays: 'The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain You, much less this temple I have built' (1 Kings 8:27).

**Destroyed and rebuilt:** the Babylonians 'burned down the house of the LORD' (2 Kings 25:9), and the returned exiles built it again: 'this temple was completed on the third day of the month of Adar' (Ezra 6:15).

**In the Gospels** Jesus teaches in its courts and 'drove all from the temple courts' (John 2:15); at his death 'the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom' (Matthew 27:51).

**Where readers differ.** Some passages are read in more than one way: the temple in them has been understood as the building that stood in Jerusalem when the passage was written, a temple yet to be built, a temple in heaven, the people of God, or a figure of something else. The site shows these verses and does not choose among the readings: 2 Thessalonians 2:4, of the one called 'the man of lawlessness' in verse 3, 'So he will seat himself in the temple of God, proclaiming himself to be God'; Matthew 24:15; Haggai 2:9; Ezekiel 40-48, the temple the prophet is shown 'in visions of God' (40:2); Revelation 11:1-2; and Zechariah 6:12-15.

temptation.desc:
'Consider it pure joy, my brothers, when you encounter trials of many kinds' (Jas 1:2).

The word covers both trial and enticement in this translation and the text does not always mark which. James 1:2 is plainly the first, James 1:14 plainly the second, and they are eleven verses apart in one letter.

ten_commandments.name: the Ten Commandments
ten_commandments.desc:
'And God spoke all these words' (Exod 20:1), and the text names them at Exod 34:28: 'He wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant — the Ten Commandments.'

Named by the text, which is why they are here when the Sermon on the Mount is recorded only as the frame its verses share. Deuteronomy 4:13 and 10:4 name them again.

The text does not number them. How the ten divide is itself disputed between traditions — where the first ends and the second begins, and whether coveting is one commandment or two — and the text supplies the total without supplying the division.

Her name is used as a type nine centuries after her death, of somebody in a church in Asia Minor. It is one of very few places Scripture turns a person into a category, and it does it without explaining the reference.

The end recorded of her is exact and was announced in advance: 'The dogs will devour Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel' (1Kgs 21:23), and 2 Kings 9:33 reports it.

**The deliverance is stated as not being by the deliverer.** David says it before the fight and gives the reason for saying it: the assembly is to know something, and what they are to know is where the saving comes from.

v37 has the word twice already -- 'The LORD, who delivered me from the claws of the lion and the bear, will deliver me from the hand of this Philistine' -- and reasons from two past deliverances to a third.

the_blood.name: the blood
the_blood.desc:
**A hundred and one verses say 'the blood of', and ninety-two of them are outside the gospels.** It is a word the law and the letters share and the narrative barely touches.

Leviticus states the principle -- 'the life of the flesh is in the blood ... it is the blood that makes atonement for the soul' (17:11) -- and Hebrews restates it as a rule: 'without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness' (9:22).

Hebrews then turns it on the whole sacrificial system: 'He did not enter by the blood of goats and calves, but He entered the Most Holy Place once for all by His own blood' (9:12). **Not more blood, and not different blood, but the last of it** -- which is the argument the epistle exists to make.

Revelation keeps it and makes it a means of victory: 'They have conquered him by the blood of the Lamb' (12:11).

the_burning_fiery_furnace.name: the blazing fiery furnace
the_burning_fiery_furnace.desc: Heated 'seven times hotter than usual', which kills the men who carry them to it. Daniel 3:27 is careful about the result: the fire had no power on their bodies, Not a hair of their heads was singed, their robes were unaffected, and there was no smell of fire on them.

the_candlestick.desc: Beaten from one piece of pure gold, seven lamps, almond-shaped bowls. Zechariah 4 sees it again with two olive trees beside it and asks what it means; the answer given there is 'Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit'.

the_capture_of_lot.name: the capture of Lot
the_capture_of_lot.desc: Abram heard that his relative had been captured.

the_censer.name: the censer
the_censer.desc: A fire pan for incense, and Scripture almost always brings it up when someone is using it who should not be. Nadab and Abihu with strange fire, Korah's two hundred and fifty, Uzziah in the temple. Revelation 8:5 fills one with fire from the altar and casts it at the earth.

the_chaff_which_the_wind_drives_away.name: chaff driven off by the wind
the_chaff_which_the_wind_drives_away.desc:
'Not so the wicked! For they are like chaff driven off by the wind.' (Ps 1:4).

The answer to the verse before it. Psalm 1 sets a tree planted by rivers of water against chaff with nothing under it, and the whole psalm is those two pictures.

the_comforter.name: the Advocate
the_comforter.desc:
'I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate to be with you forever' (John 14:16).

Four verses, all in one discourse, and John 14:26 states the identification outright: 'the Advocate, the Holy Spirit'. No reader has to supply it, which is unusual for this material.

Another Advocate is doing quiet work in 14:16 — it implies a first, and the speaker is the one about to leave. John 16:7 makes the departure the condition: 'Unless I go away, the Advocate will not come to you'. The text records the word and not the inference.

the_cretians_are_liars_speech.desc: As one of their own prophets has said, Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy gluttons.

the_den_of_lions.desc: Sealed with the king's own signet and the signet of his lords, so that 'nothing concerning Daniel could be changed' -- the seal binds the king as much as the stone binds Daniel. Darius spends the night fasting and comes at dawn to ask whether it worked.

the_devil.desc: The adversary; disputed with Michael, and walks about as a roaring lion. Job and Zechariah call him הַשָּׂטָן, 'the adversary', with the article (Job 1:6, Zech 3:1), which the Berean renders 'Satan'; Revelation joins the names: 'that ancient serpent called the devil and Satan' (Rev 12:9).

the_devils_also_believe_and_tremble.name: Even the demons believe that-and shudder
the_devils_also_believe_and_tremble.desc:
'You believe that God is one. Good for you! Even the demons believe that—and shudder.' (Jas 2:19).

The text sets a limit on its own most-repeated verb. What is affirmed is granted — 'Good for you' — and then shown to be shared by parties nobody would call saved. It stands three verses before 'a man is justified by his deeds and not by faith alone' (Jas 2:24).

the_diadem.name: the turban
the_diadem.desc: Four verses and never on an actual head. Job wears judgement as one; Isaiah 62:3 has Zion be one, held in the hand of God rather than worn; Ezekiel 21:26 removes it. The word only ever appears where something else is being called one.

the_disciple_whom_jesus_loved.name: the disciple whom Jesus loved
the_disciple_whom_jesus_loved.desc:
'One of His disciples, the one whom Jesus loved, was reclining at His side' (John 13:23), and again at 19:26, 20:2, 21:7 and 21:20. **John names him five times and never names him.**

He outruns Peter to the empty tomb and goes in second (20:4-8); he is the one who recognises Jesus on the shore (21:7); and the book closes by making him its author: 'This is the disciple who testifies to these things and who has written them down. And we know that his testimony is true' (21:24).

**He is traditionally identified with John son of Zebedee**, and the identification is not made anywhere in the text -- John's gospel never names either of Zebedee's sons individually, which is part of why the reading is drawn. It is recorded as a reading and not as data; `john_son_of_zebedee` is a separate id resting on the verses that name him.

the_door.name: the gate
the_door.desc: 'I am the gate. If anyone enters through Me, he will be saved. He will come in and go out and find pasture.' (John 10:9).

the_draught_of_fishes.name: the catch of fishes
the_draught_of_fishes.desc: Told twice with the detail reversed: in Luke the net breaks, in John 'but even with so many, the net was not torn'.

the_elder.name: the elder
the_elder.desc: 'The elder, To the chosen lady and her children' (2 John 1:1); 'The elder, To the beloved Gaius' (3 John 1:1).

the_eldest_brothers_house.name: the oldest brother’s house
the_eldest_brothers_house.desc: The house of Job's eldest son, where the feast was held and which the great wind struck (Job 1:13, 1:19).

the_ephod.name: the ephod
the_ephod.desc: The high priest's shoulder garment, with the twelve tribes cut into two onyx stones on the shoulder straps so that Aaron 'is to bear their names on his two shoulders as a memorial before the LORD'. Also worn plain and linen by the boy Samuel and by David dancing before the ark.

the_ephod_of_gideon.name: the ephod Gideon made
the_ephod_of_gideon.desc: Made from the golden earrings of the Midianite spoil and set up in Ophrah. Held apart from the priestly ephod because it is a different object and the verse that reports it also passes sentence on it: 'all Israel prostituted themselves by worshiping it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and his household.'

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: there he called upon the name of the LORD

the_eye_of_a_needle.name: the eye of a needle
the_eye_of_a_needle.desc:
'it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God' (Matt 19:24).

**The disciples' reaction shows how the figure was heard**: they were 'greatly astonished and asked, Who then can be saved?' (19:25), which is not the reaction to a merely difficult thing.

The answer given moves it off the man entirely: 'With man this is impossible, but with God all things are possible' (19:26). *The one verse a reader usually remembers is the one before that.*

the_fate_of_the_wicked.name: the fate of the wicked
the_fate_of_the_wicked.desc: Bildad's repeated description of the destruction awaiting the wicked man.

the_father.name: the Father
the_father.desc:
'you have one Father, who is in heaven' (Matt 23:9).

Held apart from God on purpose, and the reason is mechanical rather than doctrinal. The text distinguishes Jesus from the Father in some verses and from God in others, and folded into one those two sets become indistinguishable. Separated, the pattern is visible and a reader can check it: of the fifteen statements setting Jesus apart, six name the Father, seven name God, and two name both — and three of the seven address or name the Father in the same breath (John 17:3, Eph 1:17, John 20:17).

Every relation here points at whichever one its verse actually names. Nothing is normalised, because the normalising is the thing under examination.
aka: the Father which is in heaven

the_father_draws_him.name: except the Father draw him
the_father_draws_him.desc:
'No one can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him, and I will raise him up at the last day.' (John 6:44).

The mirror of John 14:6, and between them they close a circle: no one reaches the Father except by the Son, and no one reaches the Son unless the Father draws him. The text states both and does not comment on the shape they make together.

The next verse softens the mechanism into hearing: 'Everyone who has heard the Father and learned from Him comes to Me' (6:45). Whether draw and hear and learn are one act is the whole of a long argument, and this carries the two verses and no verdict.

items.label: draws on
items.name: No one comes to the Father

the_father_loves_the_son.name: The Father loves the Son
the_father_loves_the_son.desc:
'The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in His hands.' (John 3:35), and again at 5:20 with a different verb of showing.

John 5:19-26 is the densest statement in Scripture of what the Father does and what the Son does, and every clause runs one way: 'The Son can do nothing by Himself, unless He sees the Father doing it' (5:19); 'the Father judges no one, but has assigned all judgment to the Son' (5:22); 'as the Father has life in Himself, so also He has granted the Son to have life in Himself' (5:26).

The passage is cited by every side of the argument about what the two are to one another, because it makes the Son's authority total and its source external in the same breath. The text records the clauses and joins none of them into a conclusion.

items.name: Does Job fear God for nothing?

the_fear_of_the_lord.name: the fear of the LORD
the_fear_of_the_lord.desc:
'The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge' (Prov 1:7).

Thirty verses, and twenty-nine of them are in the Old Testament. Fourteen in Proverbs, six in Isaiah, four in 2 Chronicles, three in the Psalms. The single New Testament use is Acts 9:31, where the churches walk in it. A vocabulary that belongs almost entirely to one half of Scripture, in the way trust does and faith does not.

And the text defines it nine times, differently each time.

    Ps 19:9      is clean, enduring for ever
    Ps 111:10    the beginning of wisdom
    Prov 1:7     the beginning of knowledge
    Prov 8:13    is to hate evil
    Prov 14:26   is strong confidence
    Prov 14:27   a fountain of life
    Prov 15:33   the instruction of wisdom
    Isa 33:6     is his treasure
    Job 28:28    that is wisdom

Nine predicates for one subject, and no verse reconciles them. Two of the nine put it at the beginning of something — which is where it earns its place as a candidate for the text's declared entry point rather than a computed one.

Held apart from fear. Nothing in that list is said of being afraid. It is clean, it is a treasure, it is strong confidence, and it is a fountain of life; the text's other fear is what perfect love casts out (1John 4:18). The words are shared and the uses are not, which is why this is a concept of its own and not a qualified instance of the other.

the_fear_of_the_lord_is_a_fountain_of_li.name: The fear of the Lord is a fountain of life
the_fear_of_the_lord_is_a_fountain_of_li.desc:
'The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning a man from the snares of death.' (Prov 14:27), immediately after 'He who fears the LORD is secure in confidence, and his children shall have a place of refuge.' (Prov 14:26).

Two definitions in consecutive verses, and both are about safety rather than knowledge -- confidence, refuge, a fountain, escape from snares. The verses either side of them in the same chapter are the ones usually quoted about wisdom.

items.label: is likened to
items.name: The fear of the LORD is pure, enduring forever

the_fear_of_the_lord_is_clean.name: The fear of the LORD is pure, enduring forever
the_fear_of_the_lord_is_clean.desc:
'The fear of the LORD is pure, enduring forever; the judgments of the LORD are true, being altogether righteous.' (Ps 19:9).

The sixth of six statements in Ps 19:7-9, each naming a thing of the LORD and what it is: the law perfect, the testimony sure, the statutes right, the commandment pure, the fear clean, the judgments true. It is listed among things given rather than among things felt, which is the clearest single reason to hold it apart from fear.

items.label: is used as an image for
items.name: The fear of the Lord is a fountain of life

the_fear_of_the_lord_is_the_beginning_of.name: the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom
the_fear_of_the_lord_is_the_beginning_of.desc:
'The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom' (Prov 9:10), and the identical sentence at Psalm 111:10, with Proverbs 1:7 reading 'knowledge' for 'wisdom'.

**Three books, one formula, and no verse marks the repetition.** It is the clearest case in the wisdom literature of a saying circulating rather than being composed once.

items.label: is used as an image for
items.name: the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom

the_fear_of_the_lord_is_to_hate_evil.name: To fear the LORD is to hate evil
the_fear_of_the_lord_is_to_hate_evil.desc:
'To fear the LORD is to hate evil; I hate arrogant pride, evil conduct, and perverse speech.' (Prov 8:13).

The only one of the nine definitions that names what is hated, and it names four things: pride, arrogancy, the evil way, perverse speech. The verse then shifts speaker -- 'do I hate' -- so the hating is attributed rather than left general.

the_fear_of_the_lord_that_is_wisdom.name: the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom
the_fear_of_the_lord_that_is_wisdom.desc:
'And He said to man, Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, and to turn away from evil is understanding.' (Job 28:28).

The end of a chapter asking where wisdom is found, which has just said that it is not in the deep, not in the sea, and cannot be bought with gold. The answer given is not a place.

Said as an identity rather than a beginning -- Proverbs and the Psalm make it where wisdom starts, Job makes it what wisdom is.

items.label: is likened to
items.name: the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom

the_feast_at_the_eldest_brothers_house.name: the feast at the oldest brother’s house
the_feast_at_the_eldest_brothers_house.desc: while Job's sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother's house

the_field_of_isaacs_meditation.name: the field
the_field_of_isaacs_meditation.desc: The field where Isaac went to meditate in the early evening (Gen 24:63).

a_pattern_of_the_one_to_come.name: a pattern of the One to come
a_pattern_of_the_one_to_come.desc:
'death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who did not sin in the way that Adam transgressed. He is a pattern of the One to come.' (Rom 5:14).

Scripture names its own typology. Everywhere else a reader has to notice that one figure stands for another; here Paul says it in the sentence, and the man he says it of is the first one in the book.

The comparison is then built by contrast rather than resemblance: 'For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous' (5:19). The two are alike in shape and opposite in content, which is the whole argument of the passage.

the_fire_of_god.name: the fire of God
the_fire_of_god.desc: The fire of God fell from heaven. It burned and consumed the sheep and the servants

the_first_and_the_last.name: the first and the last
the_first_and_the_last.desc: 'Do not be afraid. I am the First and the Last,' (Rev 1:17), and again at 22:13 with 'I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End'.

the_first_man_and_the_last_adam.name: the first man Adam, the last Adam
the_first_man_and_the_last_adam.desc:
'The first man Adam became a living being”; the last Adam a life-giving spirit.' (1Cor 15:45), and 'The first man was of the dust of the earth, the second man from heaven' (15:47).

Adam's name is given to somebody else. Not like Adam, not a second Adam — the last Adam, as though the name were an office rather than a person. It is the same move Scripture makes with David at Ezekiel 34:23, and this one is in the New Testament and about Christ.

'For as in Adam all die, so in Christ all will be made alive' (15:22) states the parallel as a pair of memberships. What all covers in each half is read differently by different traditions and the text does not settle it.
