the_flame_shall_dry_up_his_branches.desc: the flame will wither his shoots

the_fleece_of_wool.name: a fleece of wool on the threshing floor
the_fleece_of_wool.desc:
'behold, I will place a fleece of wool on the threshing floor. If there is dew only on the fleece and all the ground is dry, then I will know that You are going to save Israel by my hand' (Judg 6:37).

He asks twice, and the second time he reverses it — dry fleece, wet ground — and apologises for asking: 'Do not be angry with me' (6:39). The text records the asking, the apology and the granting, and passes no comment on any of them.

the_flood.name: the flood
the_flood.desc: The forty-day flood sent upon the earth; 'For forty days the flood kept coming on the earth' (Gen 7:17).

the_food.name: the food
the_food.desc: all the food of the seven years, gathered and laid up in the cities.

the_foremost.name: the one in the lead
the_foremost.desc: Unnamed; "He instructed the one in the lead" (Gen 32:17).

the_fourth_looks_like_a_son_of_the_gods.name: the fourth looks like a son of the gods!
the_fourth_looks_like_a_son_of_the_gods.desc: Nebuchadnezzar's words, and the text leaves them his: he says what the fourth figure looks like to him and the narrative does not confirm or correct it. At 3:28 he calls the same figure an angel.

the_four.name: the four
the_four.desc: The four men who bore the paralytic: "Then a paralytic was brought to Him, carried by four men"; they uncover and break up the roof and let down the bed.

the_four_horses.name: the white, red, black and pale horses
the_four_horses.desc:
A white horse whose rider has a bow and a crown and goes 'to overcome and conquer' (Rev 6:2); a red horse whose rider takes peace from the earth (6:4); a black horse whose rider has 'a pair of scales' (6:5); and a pale horse (6:8).

Only the fourth rider is named: 'Its rider's name was Death, and Hades followed close behind' (6:8). The other three are described by what they carry and what they do, and the text never says who they are.

The first is the contested one. A crown, a bow, and conquering — and readers have taken him for Christ, for conquest, and for a counterfeit, on the strength of a white horse appearing again at 19:11 with a rider who is named. The text holds both verses and declines to join them.

items.label: took
items.name: the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah

the_friend_of_god.name: a friend of God
the_friend_of_god.desc:
'And the Scripture was fulfilled that says, “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness,” and he was called a friend of God.' (Jas 2:23).

Three books call him it and none of them is Genesis. Isaiah 41:8, 2 Chronicles 20:7 and James 2:23 — and James says he was called, without saying by whom or where. It is a title Scripture attributes to itself and cannot locate.

the_glorious_appearing.name: glorious appearance of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ
the_glorious_appearing.desc: 'glorious appearance of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ' (Titus 2:13)

the_god_of_all_grace.name: the God of all grace
the_god_of_all_grace.desc:
'And after you have suffered for a little while, the God of all grace, who has called you to His eternal glory in Christ, will Himself restore you, secure you, strengthen you, and establish you.' (1Pet 5:10).

**Four concepts in one sentence and an order imposed on them**: grace, glory, suffering, strength -- with the suffering placed before the strengthening and given a duration, *a while*.

the_god_of_beth_el.name: the God of Bethel
the_god_of_beth_el.desc: God names himself so: 'I am the God of Bethel'.

the_golden_pot_of_manna.name: the golden pot of manna
the_golden_pot_of_manna.desc: An omer of manna laid before the LORD to be preserved. Hebrews 9:4 puts it inside the ark with Aaron’s staff that had budded, and the stone tablets of the covenant -- one verse naming four objects at once.

the_golden_bowls_full_of_incense.name: golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints
the_golden_bowls_full_of_incense.desc:
'Each one had a harp, and they were holding golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints.' (Rev 5:8).

Another stated key, and an unusually gentle one in a book of beasts and seals: the incense is prayer, said plainly, in a relative clause. It is repeated at 8:3-4 with the smoke ascending 'with the prayers of the saints ... before God'.

The figure rests on the altar of incense in the tabernacle, and Revelation is where the text finally says what that was for.

the_good_shepherd.name: the good shepherd
the_good_shepherd.desc: Claimed at John 10:11; The good shepherd lays down His life for the sheep.

items.label: is drawn on by
items.name: Greater love has no one than this

items.label: is drawn on by
items.name: My sheep listen to My voice

i_do_not_do_the_good_i_want_to_do.name: I do not do the good I want to do
i_do_not_do_the_good_i_want_to_do.desc:
'For I do not do the good I want to do. Instead, I keep on doing the evil I do not want to do.' (Rom 7:19), stated first at v15 and again as a discovery at v21: 'So this is the principle I have discovered: When I want to do good, evil is right there with me'

The division is inside one person and the pronoun never changes. It is not that he does not know what is right, nor that he does not want it -- 'I have the desire to do what is good, but I cannot carry it out' (v18).

items.label: is a core concept of the major theme
items.name: Sin / Exile / Death (major theme)

the_gospel_of_the_kingdom_of_god.name: the gospel of God
the_gospel_of_the_kingdom_of_god.desc: "proclaimed the gospel of God" (Mark 1:14). The ASV, BSB and YLT read only 'the gospel of God' here.

the_grave.name: the grave
the_grave.desc: The place of the dead, where the weary rest and the wicked cease troubling.

the_great_dragon_that_old_serpent.name: the great dragon, that old serpent
the_great_dragon_that_old_serpent.desc:
'And the great dragon was hurled down-that ancient serpent called the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world.' (Rev 12:9), and the same four names again at 20:2.

Four names in one clause, twice. It is the most explicit identification of a figure anywhere in Scripture — dragon, serpent, Devil, Satan, stated as one, with no room left for a reader to do the joining.

Old is doing quiet work: it points back at Genesis 3 without citing it, and Genesis never calls the serpent any of the other three names.

the_great_feast_of_isaacs_weaning.name: a great feast
the_great_feast_of_isaacs_weaning.desc: Abraham held a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.

the_great_god_and_our_savior.name: our great God and Savior Jesus Christ
the_great_god_and_our_savior.desc: 'our great God and Savior Jesus Christ' (Titus 2:13)

the_great_wind.name: the great wind from the wilderness
the_great_wind.desc: a mighty wind swept in from the desert and struck the four corners of the house

the_greatest_man_of_all_the_people_of_th.name: the greatest man of all the people of the East

the_ground.name: the ground
the_ground.desc: the ground, cursed for Adam's sake and the ground to which man returns (Gen 3:17, 3:19); distinct from the concept 'ground'.

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: May this one comfort us in the labor and toil of our hands caused by the ground that the LORD has cursed

the_half_of_my_goods_i_give_to_the_poor.name: half of my possessions I give to the poor
the_half_of_my_goods_i_give_to_the_poor.desc:
'Look, Lord, half of my possessions I give to the poor, and if I have cheated anyone, I will repay it fourfold.' (Luke 19:8).

**He is not asked for any of it.** Nothing has been required, and the fourfold restitution he offers is the law's penalty for stealing a sheep -- he applies the harshest available measure to himself.

The tree is the detail everyone keeps: 'he ran on ahead and climbed a sycamore tree to see Him' (19:4), because he was short and the crowd was in the way.

the_heavens.name: the heavens
the_heavens.desc: the plural heavens of Genesis 2:1 and 2:4, made by the Lord God; distinct from the singular expanse/heaven.

the_high.name: those on high
the_high.desc: The lofty ones whom God judges (Job 21:22).

the_high_priest.name: the high priest
the_high_priest.desc: The office named in "During the high priesthood of Abiathar".

the_hireling_flees.name: the hired hand runs away
the_hireling_flees.desc: Set against the good shepherd by what he owns: 'whose own the sheep are not'. The failure is contractual before it is moral.

the_holy_one_of_god.name: the Holy One of God
the_holy_one_of_god.desc: The title cried out in the synagogue at Capernaum: "I know who You are — the Holy One of God". Kept apart from the existing title `the_holy_one` pending a decision.

items.label: is a title of
items.name: Jesus
items.claimed_by_name: the man with an unclean spirit

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: I know who You are-the Holy One of God!

the_house_at_capernaum.name: home
the_house_at_capernaum.desc: The house in Capernaum where Jesus was: "the people heard that He was home".

the_house_built_upon_a_rock.name: the house built upon a rock
the_house_built_upon_a_rock.desc: Both houses get the same storm. The parable turns on the foundation and not on the weather, and the two builders are told apart by doing rather than hearing.

the_image_of_god.name: the image of God
the_image_of_god.desc: The verse says 'who is the image of God'.

the_imprisonment_of_john_the_baptist.name: John put in prison
the_imprisonment_of_john_the_baptist.desc: "After the arrest of John" -- Mark dates the beginning of Jesus's Galilean preaching from it and names no captor here.

the_inhabitants_thereof.name: those who dwell in them
the_inhabitants_thereof.desc: the inhabitants of the waters, in Job's speech

our_inner_self_is_being_renewed_day_by_d.name: our inner self is being renewed day by day
our_inner_self_is_being_renewed_day_by_d.desc:
'Therefore we do not lose heart. Though our outer self is wasting away, yet our inner self is being renewed day by day.' (2Cor 4:16).

Two things happening at once in one person and in opposite directions, which is the same shape as 'I have been crucified with Christ, and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me' (Gal 2:20) and 'as living sacrifices' (Rom 12:1). The renewal is dated -- day by day -- and the perishing is not.

the_joy_of_the_lord_is_your_strength.name: the joy of the LORD is your strength
the_joy_of_the_lord_is_your_strength.desc:
'since today is holy to our Lord. Do not grieve, for the joy of the LORD is your strength.' (Neh 8:10).

One of the few places the text explains one of these words by another. It is said to a crowd that has just heard the law read and started weeping, which is the reason for the instruction not to be sorry.

the_jubile.name: the Jubilee
the_jubile.desc: Every fiftieth year: debts released, land returned, servants freed. No narrative anywhere records it being kept. It is held the way the day of atonement is held — as a commanded observance — and that a command has no observance narrative behind it is a fact about the text, not a gap in the text.

the_judge_of_all_the_earth.name: the Judge of all the earth

the_just_shall_live_by_his_faith.name: the righteous will live by faith
the_just_shall_live_by_his_faith.desc:
'the righteous will live by faith' (Hab 2:4).

Eight words in a minor prophet, quoted three times in the New Testament, and the engine of the Reformation. Romans 1:17, Galatians 3:11 and Hebrews 10:38 all cite it, and each puts the emphasis in a different place — the just, or shall live, or by faith.

In Habakkuk it answers a complaint about violence going unpunished. The prophet has asked how long, been told the Chaldeans are coming, and objected that the cure is worse than the disease. This is part of the reply, and the text records where it sits before recording where it went.

the_keeper_of_the_prison.name: the prison warden
the_keeper_of_the_prison.desc: the keeper of the prison in Joseph's time

the_key_of_david.name: the key of David
the_key_of_david.desc:
'who holds the key of David. What He opens no one can shut' (Rev 3:7).

Lifted from Isaiah 22:22 almost word for word, where it is said of Eliakim, a steward given authority over a household: 'I will place on his shoulder the key to the house of David. What he opens no one can shut'. Revelation drops the house of and keeps everything else.

Scripture holds both verses and does not say what the reuse means.

the_keys_of_the_kingdom.name: the keys of the kingdom of heaven
the_keys_of_the_kingdom.desc:
'I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven. Whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven' (Matt 16:19).

The binding half is said again two chapters later to everybody: 'whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven' (Matt 18:18), plural, with no keys attached. Scripture holds both verses and does not say what the difference between them is.

the_kingdom_of_god.name: the kingdom of God
the_kingdom_of_god.desc: The settled phrase Jesus preaches: "the kingdom of God is at hand".

items.label: is built from the words
items.name: the mystery of the kingdom of God

the_kinsman_redeemer.name: the kinsman that has right to redeem
the_kinsman_redeemer.desc:
'The man is a close relative. He is one of our kinsman-redeemers.' (Ruth 2:20), and the transaction itself: 'Ruth the Moabitess ... I have acquired Ruth the Moabitess, Mahlon's widow, as my wife, to raise up the name of the deceased through his inheritance' (4:10).

It is a legal provision before it is anything else — Leviticus 25:25 sets it out, a relative buying back what a poor man had to sell. Ruth is Scripture's one worked example of it, with the shoe changing hands and a nearer kinsman declining first.

Readers take it as a figure and the text does not say so. Job 19:25 uses the same word — 'I know that my Redeemer lives' — and the text holds the legal sense and the redemption concept as separate meanings joined by the verses, not merged.

the_land_not_theirs.name: a land that is not their own
the_land_not_theirs.desc: the unnamed land where the seed shall be strangers

a_land_of_darkness_and_gloom.name: a land of darkness and gloom
a_land_of_darkness_and_gloom.desc: Quote: 'to a land of darkness and gloom' (10:21); 'A land of darkness' (10:22)

the_laver.name: the basin
the_laver.desc: A bronze basin for washing, set between the tabernacle and the altar. Exodus 38:8 says what it was made from: 'the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting'.

the_law_is_holy.name: the law is holy
the_law_is_holy.desc:
'So then, the law is holy, and the commandment is holy, righteous, and good.' (Rom 7:12), and 'the law is spiritual; but I am unspiritual, sold as a slave to sin.' (Rom 7:14).

**The verdict that stops the chapter being read as an attack on the law.** Four adjectives in one sentence, none qualified. Whatever has gone wrong in Romans 7, the text does not locate it in the law -- v14 puts it in the other party.

the_law_of_the_lord_is_perfect.name: The Law of the LORD is perfect, reviving the soul
the_law_of_the_lord_is_perfect.desc:
'The Law of the LORD is perfect, reviving the soul; the testimony of the LORD is trustworthy, making wise the simple.' (Ps 19:7).

Six statements in three verses, each naming a thing of the LORD and what it does. This is the first, and its verb is the one Ps 23:3 uses of the shepherd.

the_law_of_the_spirit_of_life.name: the law of the Spirit of life
the_law_of_the_spirit_of_life.desc:
'For in Christ Jesus the law of the Spirit of life set you free from the law of sin and death.' (Rom 8:2).

Two laws in one sentence, both named as laws and set against each other. The chapter opens on this contrast and works it out through flesh and Spirit for the next eleven verses.

items.label: draws on
items.name: with my mind I serve the law of God

the_life_was_the_light_of_men.name: that life was the light of men
the_life_was_the_light_of_men.desc:
'In Him was life, and that life was the light of men. The Light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it' (John 1:4-5).

**Genesis 1's first two things, in Genesis 1's order, with an outcome added.** There the light is made and divided from the darkness; here it shines in the darkness and is not comprehended. Neither the making nor the dividing is mentioned; what is carried over is the pair.

The chain of identifications runs life, then light, then -- at v9 -- 'the true Light'.

the_light.name: the light
the_light.desc: The light that God caused to be at the command 'Let there be light', distinct from the concept of light in general.

the_light_is_as_darkness.name: even the light is like darkness
the_light_is_as_darkness.desc: Quote: 'where even the light is like darkness'

the_line_of_scarlet_thread.name: this scarlet cord in the window
the_line_of_scarlet_thread.desc:
'you have tied this scarlet cord in the window through which you let us down' (Josh 2:18).

The sign is the rope she used to save them, kept in place to save her. The text makes nothing further of the colour.

Hebrews 11 and James 2 both name her, as both name Abraham: Hebrews for her faith, 'By faith the prostitute Rahab ... did not perish' (Heb 11:31), James for her actions, 'was not even Rahab the prostitute justified by her actions' (Jas 2:25). Matthew 1:5 names a Rahab in the genealogy; the text does not say it is she.

the_lion_has_prevailed_and_a_lamb_stood.name: behold the Lion ... a Lamb who appeared to have been slain
the_lion_has_prevailed_and_a_lamb_stood.desc:
'Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has triumphed to open the scroll' (Rev 5:5) — and what John then turns and sees is not a lion: 'Then I saw a Lamb who appeared to have been slain, standing in the center of the throne' (5:6).

The announcement and the sight do not match, and the text does not remark on it. He is told a lion has conquered and shown a killed lamb, in consecutive verses, and the book proceeds as though these were the same thing.

It is the clearest instance in Scripture of a figure being corrected by the next figure rather than explained, and any reading of Revelation has to account for it.

items.label: is drawn on by
items.name: the Lion of the tribe of Judah

items.label: is drawn on by
items.name: the root and the offspring of David

the_little_book_eaten.name: the little book that was eaten
the_little_book_eaten.desc: Ezekiel is handed a roll and told to eat it, and it is 'as sweet as honey in my mouth'. John is handed a little book by an angel and told the same thing: sweet as honey in the mouth, and 'when I had eaten it, my stomach turned bitter'. Held as one record because the second repeats the first almost exactly and then adds what happens next.

the_lord_gave_and_the_lord_has_taken_awa.name: the LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away
the_lord_gave_and_the_lord_has_taken_awa.desc:
'Naked I came from my mother's womb, and naked I will return. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed be the name of the LORD' (Job 1:21).

He attributes both halves to the same source and blesses him for the pair, which is what the next verse singles out: 'In all this, Job did not sin or charge God with wrongdoing' (1:22).

The book then spends thirty-five chapters on him charging God with a good deal, and the text does not treat that as a contradiction of this verse.

items.label: is a core concept of the major theme
items.name: Wisdom Literature (poetic Theology) (major theme)

the_lord_is_my_shepherd.name: the LORD is my shepherd
the_lord_is_my_shepherd.desc:
'The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.' (Ps 23:1).

**Written, by its own superscription, by a shepherd** -- and the psalm puts him on the other side of the figure. He is the sheep in it.

The best-known verse in it changes person: the psalm speaks *about* the shepherd until the valley, and then speaks *to* him -- 'for You are with me' (23:4). That turn is the construction this project has found again and again in the verses people memorise.

items.label: is used as an image for
items.name: led by the Spirit

items.label: is used as an image for
items.name: My sheep listen to My voice

items.label: is used as an image for
items.name: The Law of the LORD is perfect, reviving the soul

items.label: draws on
items.name: You anoint my head with oil

items.label: is likened to
items.name: Do not be afraid, for I am with you

items.label: is likened to
items.name: In My Father's house are many rooms

the_lord_merciful_and_gracious.name: The LORD, the LORD God, is compassionate and gracious
the_lord_merciful_and_gracious.desc:
'Then the LORD passed in front of Moses and called out: The LORD, the LORD God, is compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion and faithfulness,' (Exod 34:6), continuing 'Yet He will by no means leave the guilty unpunished' (34:7).

The most travelled formula in Scripture. It is taken up at Nehemiah 9:17, Psalm 86:15, Psalm 103:8, Psalm 145:8, Joel 2:13 and Jonah 4:2 — one verse across four genres.

Jonah is the sharpest of the six. He quotes it as a complaint: he fled because he knew God was merciful and gracious and would relent, which is the formula used against the outcome it usually comforts. The second half travels less than the first, and which portion a later writer takes is worth watching.

the_lord_spoke_unto_moses_face_to_face.name: the LORD would speak to Moses face to face
the_lord_spoke_unto_moses_face_to_face.desc:
'Thus the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend.' (Exod 33:11).

Twenty-nine verses later the same chapter says he could not: 'You cannot see My face, for no one can see Me and live' (33:20). Scripture puts both in one chapter and does not reconcile them.

Deuteronomy 34:10 makes it the thing that was never repeated: 'Since that time, no prophet has risen in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face'.

the_lost_piece_of_silver.name: the lost coin
the_lost_piece_of_silver.desc: The middle of three in Luke 15, between the lost sheep and the lost son, and the only one where the thing lost cannot look for itself.

the_man_slain_by_lamech.name: the man Lamech said he slew
the_man_slain_by_lamech.desc: Unnamed man, spoken of by Lamech as 'a man to my wounding'.

the_man_who_wrestled_with_jacob.name: a man
the_man_who_wrestled_with_jacob.desc: Unnamed; "there a man wrestled with him until daybreak" (Gen 32:24).

items.label: asserts
items.name: Let me go, for it is daybreak.

items.label: told
items.name: Let me go, for it is daybreak.

the_marked_animals_removed.name: the marked animals removed
the_marked_animals_removed.desc: all the streaked or spotted male goats and every speckled or spotted female goat — every one that had any white on it — and every dark-colored lamb

items.label: told
items.name: The men of Sodom demand the angels

items.label: told
items.name: The men of Sodom threaten Lot

items.label: asserts
items.name: The men of Sodom demand the angels

items.label: asserts
items.name: The men of Sodom threaten Lot

the_men_of_that_place.name: the men of that place
the_men_of_that_place.desc: The men whom Hirah asked: 'the men of that place' (Gen 38:21).

items.label: asserts
items.name: No shrine prostitute has been here

items.label: told
items.name: No shrine prostitute has been here

the_mercy_seat.name: the mercy seat
the_mercy_seat.desc: Hebrews 9:5 names it with one Greek word, ἱλαστήριον. Exodus 25:22 is what the object is for: 'There I will meet with you, and I will tell you from above the mercy seat'.

the_midwife.name: the midwife
the_midwife.desc: the midwife who said unto Rachel, Do not be afraid, for you are having another son (Gen 35:17)

items.label: asserts
items.name: Do not be afraid, for you are having another son

items.label: told
items.name: Do not be afraid, for you are having another son

the_miserable_and_bitter.name: them that are in misery and bitter in soul
the_miserable_and_bitter.desc: Those who long for death and rejoice when they find the grave.

the_mitre.name: the turban
the_mitre.desc: The high priest's linen headdress, carrying the golden plate on a blue lace across the forefront.

the_most_holy_place.name: the most holy place
the_most_holy_place.desc: Behind the second veil, entered once a year by one man. Hebrews argues from the restriction rather than from the room: that the way in 'had not yet been disclosed as long as the first tabernacle was still standing' (Heb 9:8).

the_mother_of_all_living.name: the mother of all the living
the_mother_of_all_living.desc:
'And Adam named his wife Eve, because she would be the mother of all the living' (Gen 3:20).

The naming comes immediately after the sentence of death. Genesis 3:19 ends with dust returning to dust and the very next verse calls her the mother of all living. The text does not comment on the order, and it is hard to read as accidental.

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: On the mountain of the LORD it will be provided

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: Your servant has indeed found favor in your sight, and you have shown me great kindness by sparing my life. But I cannot run to the mountains; the disaster will overtake me, and I will die.

the_mourners.name: the mourners
the_mourners.desc: Those who mourn, whom Job says he comforted: "as a comforter of the mourners."

the_multitude.name: the people
the_multitude.desc: The crowd that came to Jesus by the sea: "All the people came to Him, and He taught them".

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: He and His disciples could not even eat

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: Here are My mother and My brothers!

the_mystery_of_the_kingdom_of_god.name: the mystery of the kingdom of God
the_mystery_of_the_kingdom_of_god.desc: The thing said to be given to the hearers to know in Mark 4:11.

the_name_of_the_lord.name: the name of the Lord
the_name_of_the_lord.desc:
'The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous run to it and are safe.' (Prov 18:10).

A hundred and eight verses, and it behaves as a thing rather than a label: it is called upon (Gen 4:26, Joel 2:32), run into (Prov 18:10), remembered against chariots and horses (Ps 20:7), and blasphemed or hallowed. What is done to it is done to him.

The promise attached to calling on it is quoted twice in the New Testament -- Acts 2:21 and Rom 10:13 both cite Joel 2:32 -- and both times the word 'saved' replaces Joel's 'delivered'.

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: The name of the Lord is a strong tower

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: everyone who calls on the name of the LORD

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: At that time men began to call upon the name of the LORD

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: there he called upon the name of the LORD

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: He guides me in the paths of righteousness for the sake of His name

the_name_of_the_lord_is_a_strong_tower.name: The name of the Lord is a strong tower
the_name_of_the_lord_is_a_strong_tower.desc:
'The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous run to it and are safe.' (Prov 18:10).

A name given as a place, entered by running. The verse following puts a rich man's wealth in the same position -- 'his fortified city; it is like a high wall in his imagination' (Prov 18:11) -- so the figure is used twice on facing pages, once as fact and once as self-deception.

the_nation_of_ishmael.name: the nation of the slave woman's son
the_nation_of_ishmael.desc: The nation God will make of Ishmael: I will also make a nation of the slave woman’s son; I will make him into a great nation.

the_night_of_jobs_conception.name: the night of Job's conception
the_night_of_jobs_conception.desc: The night on which Job was conceived, mentioned in Job 3:3: 'the night it was said, A boy is conceived.'

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: May the day of my birth perish

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: If only darkness had taken that night away!

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: Behold, may that night be barren

the_night_vision.name: the night vision
the_night_vision.desc: The vision described in Job 4:13-16, in which a spirit appears to Eliphaz.

the_oak_beneath_bethel.name: the oak beneath Bethel
the_oak_beneath_bethel.desc: the oak under which Deborah Rebekah's nurse was buried; also called Allon-bachuth.

the_oak_by_shechem.name: the oak near Shechem
the_oak_by_shechem.desc: the oak tree under which Jacob hid the strange gods and earrings; located by Shechem.

the_old_way.name: the ancient path
the_old_way.desc: The ancient path which wicked men have trodden.

the_people.name: the nations
the_people.desc: by these He judges the nations

the_people_of_the_land.name: the people of the land
the_people_of_the_land.desc: the nation in the land not theirs, whom the seed shall serve, cited as 'them' and 'that nation'

the_people_living_in_darkness_have_seen_.name: the people living in darkness have seen a great light
the_people_living_in_darkness_have_seen_.desc:
'The people walking in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of the shadow of death, a light has dawned.' (Isa 9:2), quoted at Matt 4:16.

Matthew has them sitting where Isaiah has them walking, and applies it to Galilee at the start of the ministry. The verse two before it in Isaiah is the one about a child born and a son given.

the_pieces.name: the halves of the carcasses
the_pieces.desc: the pieces of the divided animals Abram prepared in Gen 15:10

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: the smoking furnace and burning lamp pass between the pieces

the_place_for_gold.name: a place where gold
the_place_for_gold.desc: A place where gold is fined: "a place where gold is refined".

the_place_of_understanding.name: the place of understanding
the_place_of_understanding.desc: The place where understanding resides, asked after in "where does understanding dwell?"

the_plate_of_pure_gold.name: the plate of pure gold
the_plate_of_pure_gold.desc: Engraved 'the way a gem cutter engraves a seal' with two words, and fixed to the front of the turban.
aka: the plate of the holy crown

the_poor.name: the poor
the_poor.desc: the poor of the earth (Job 24:4), who are driven out and oppressed

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: he delivers the poor in affliction

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: He does not keep the wicked alive, but He grants justice to the afflicted.

the_preacher.name: the Teacher
the_preacher.desc: Son of David, king in Jerusalem; speaks throughout Ecclesiastes.

items.label: is spoken of in

the_press.desc: The crowd at the house in Capernaum: "they gathered in such large numbers that there was no more room, not even outside the door"; called "the press" at Mark 2:4.

the_prince_of_the_devils.name: the prince of the demons
the_prince_of_the_devils.desc: The title the scribes use in their charge: "By the prince of the demons He drives out demons." (Mark 3:22).

the_ram_and_the_goat_are_named.name: the ram is Media and Persia, the goat is Greece
the_ram_and_the_goat_are_named.desc:
'The two-horned ram that you saw represents the kings of Media and Persia. The shaggy goat represents the king of Greece' (Dan 8:20-21).

The only place in Scripture where a figure is decoded into named nations. Elsewhere Daniel keeps the key general — four beasts, four kings — and here it gives three proper names in two verses. The text records that the naming happens, and nothing about what follows from it.

the_ram_of_moriah.name: the ram caught in a thicket
the_ram_of_moriah.desc: 'Then Abraham looked up and saw behind him a ram in a thicket, caught by its horns. So he went and took the ram and offered it as a burnt offering in place of his son.' (Gen 22:13). **'in place of his son' is the verse's own phrase**, and it is the whole of what the chapter says about the substitution.

the_rams.name: the males that are mating with the flock
the_rams.desc: The rams Jacob saw in the dream.

the_ravens_food.name: the raven his food
the_ravens_food.desc: The food the LORD provides for the raven: 'Who provides food for the raven?'

the_red_heifer.name: the red heifer
the_red_heifer.desc: Burnt whole outside the camp, ashes kept for a water of separation. Everyone who handles it is made unclean by the rite that makes others clean -- the priest, the burner, and the man who gathers the ashes.

the_resurrection.name: the resurrection
the_resurrection.desc: 'I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in Me will live, even though he dies.' (John 11:25), said to Martha at her brother's grave.

the_rich_man_of_luke_16.name: the rich man
the_rich_man_of_luke_16.desc: 'a rich man dressed in purple and fine linen, who lived each day in joyous splendor' (Luke 16:19). He speaks eight verses and is never named, opposite a beggar who is — the reverse of Scripture's habit, where the poor go unnamed and the rich are recorded.

the_righteous.name: the righteous
the_righteous.desc: Those upon whom the eyes of the Lord are, who cry, who have many afflictions, and whom the wicked hate (Ps 34:15,17,19,21).

items.label: is spoken of in
items.name: The righteous shall hold on his way

the_rod_of_aaron_budded.name: the rod of Aaron budded
the_rod_of_aaron_budded.desc:
'Aaron's staff, representing the house of Levi, had sprouted, put forth buds, blossomed, and produced almonds' (Num 17:8).

**The sign is a dead stick doing four things at once** -- budding, blooming and fruiting, stages that in a living tree are months apart. It settles a dispute about who may serve, and it is then kept 'as a sign for the rebellious' (17:10).

the_roll_jehoiakim_burned.name: the roll Jehoiakim burned
the_roll_jehoiakim_burned.desc: Dictated to Baruch, read to the king three or four leaves at a time, cut with a penknife and thrown on the hearth until all of it burned. Jeremiah dictates it again -- 'And many similar words were added to them'. The book that survives is longer because it was destroyed.

the_roof.name: the roof
the_roof.desc: The roof of the house at Capernaum: "they uncovered the roof above Him, made an opening".

the_root_and_offspring_of_david.name: the root and the offspring of David
the_root_and_offspring_of_david.desc: 'I, Jesus, have sent My angel to give you this testimony for the churches. I am the Root and the Offspring of David, the bright Morning Star.' (Rev 22:16). Both directions at once -- the root David came from and the offspring that came from David -- which the verse states without resolving.

items.label: draws on
items.name: behold the Lion ... a Lamb who appeared to have been slain

the_sabean_raid.name: the Sabean raid
the_sabean_raid.desc: the Sabeans swooped down and took them away

the_sacrifices_of_god_are_a_broken_spiri.name: the sacrifices of God are a broken spirit
the_sacrifices_of_god_are_a_broken_spiri.desc:
'The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, You will not despise.' (Ps 51:17), after 'You do not delight in sacrifice, or I would bring it' (51:16).

**The word is kept and its content replaced**, which is a different move from Hosea 6:6 -- Hosea sets mercy against sacrifice, and this calls the broken spirit the sacrifice.

the_same_came_to_jesus_by_night.name: He came to Jesus at night
the_same_came_to_jesus_by_night.desc:
'He came to Jesus at night and said, Rabbi, we know that You are a teacher who has come from God.' (John 3:2).

John mentions the night three times, and the third is at the burial: 'Nicodemus, who had previously come to Jesus at night, also brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about seventy-five pounds' (19:39).

The detail is carried forward deliberately across sixteen chapters, and the last time it appears the man is doing something in daylight that no one else risked. The text does not comment on the change and does not let a reader miss it.

the_same_spirit_of_faith.name: the same spirit of faith
the_same_spirit_of_faith.desc: we who have the same spirit of faith

the_scapegoat.name: the scapegoat
the_scapegoat.desc: One of two goats, chosen by lot. The other is killed; this one is kept alive, has the iniquities of Israel confessed over its head, and is led away into the wilderness. **It is the only offering in Leviticus that is not offered.**

the_sceptre.name: The scepter
the_sceptre.desc: The rod of a ruler, and in Esther the difference between living and dying: no one may approach the king unsummoned 'Only if the king extends the gold scepter may that person live'.

the_seizing_of_the_well.name: the seizing of the well
the_seizing_of_the_well.desc: The event of Abimelech's servants violently taking away the well (Gen 21:25).

the_serpent_beguiled_eve.name: the serpent deceived Eve
the_serpent_beguiled_eve.desc:
'just as Eve was deceived by the serpent's cunning, your minds may be led astray from your simple and pure devotion to Christ.' (2Cor 11:3).

Paul uses her as a warning about how persuasion works, not about who is to blame — the danger in the verse is a mind being moved off something simple. 1 Timothy 2:14 puts it differently: 'And it was not Adam who was deceived, but the woman who was deceived and fell into transgression'

Those two verses are read together and against each other, and Scripture holds both without reconciling them. Genesis 3:13 has her own account: 'The serpent deceived me ... I ate'.

the_seven.name: the seven
the_seven.desc: Seven men of honest report chosen by the disciples at Jerusalem and appointed by the apostles to oversee the daily distribution of food.

the_seven_fat_cows.desc: The first seven cows in Pharaoh's dream, which came up from the river and were eaten by the lean cows.

the_seven_good_ears.desc: The seven good heads of grain in one stalk, devoured by the thin ears.

the_seven_lean_cows.desc: The seven lean cows that came after and ate up the fat cows, remaining ugly.

the_seven_stars_are_the_angels.name: the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches
the_seven_stars_are_the_angels.desc:
'This is the mystery of the seven stars you saw in My right hand and of the seven golden lampstands: The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and the seven lampstands are the seven churches.' (Rev 1:20).

**Revelation opens by decoding two of its own figures and then decodes almost nothing else for twenty-one chapters.** A reader who takes 1:20 as a promise that the book explains itself is being misled by its first page.

The word used for the giving of the key is *mystery*, which in this corpus means a thing disclosed rather than a thing withheld.
aka: the mystery of the seven stars

items.name: the vision of the seven stars and seven lampstands

the_seven_thin_ears.name: seven heads of grain, withered, thin, and scorched by the east wind
the_seven_thin_ears.desc: The seven thin ears that sprung up after the good and devoured them.

the_sheep_and_the_goats.name: the sheep and the goats
the_sheep_and_the_goats.desc:
'whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers of Mine, you did for Me' (Matt 25:40).

The longest judgment scene in the gospels, and every criterion in it is an act: meat, drink, lodging, clothing, visiting. Nothing is asked about belief on either side, and neither group knows what it did — both ask when.

This is the strongest works-side passage in the gospels. It carries no verdict: readers who hold that faith alone justifies read the acts as the evidence rather than the ground, and the passage does not say which.

the_shepherds_at_the_well.desc: The unnamed shepherds Jacob met at the well in the field near Haran.

the_shewbread.desc: Twelve cakes set out weekly and eaten only by the priests (Lev 24:5-9). Its whole narrative weight is that the rule was broken once and the breach was later cited with approval.

the_ship.desc: The vessel Jesus taught from: "He got into a boat and sat in it" (Mark 4:1).

the_sign_of_the_prophet_jonas.desc: The only sign offered to a generation asking for one, and it is another prophet's three days. Luke 11:30 gives the comparison without the whale.

the_signet.name: seal
the_signet.desc: A seal carried on the person, standing for the authority of whoever owns it -- which is why Judah handing his over as a pledge is enough to convict him three months later, and why Jeremiah and Haggai can use one man's removal and another's appointment as the same figure run backwards.

the_son_of_david.name: the Son of David
the_son_of_david.desc:
'This is the record of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham:' (Matt 1:1) — the first line of the New Testament, and it names two ancestors and stops.

It is the crowd's word before it is a doctrine: 'Hosanna to the Son of David' (Matt 21:9), shouted at the entry into Jerusalem, and before that by two blind men who wanted mercy (9:27). It is what people call him when they want something, which is not how titles usually enter Scripture.

Matthew 22:42-45 has Jesus turn the title into a question — if David calls him Lord, how is he his son — and the text records that the question is asked and not what it settles.

the_son_of_god.name: the Son of God
the_son_of_god.desc:
The complement, and the counts invert. Son of man is 74 of 76 narrative; his Son is 18 of 21 epistolary. The gospels and the letters have different vocabulary for the same figure, and a reader moving between them is reading two idioms rather than one.

What the letters do with it is argue. Romans 1:4 makes the resurrection the declaration — 'declared to be the Son of God with power ... by the resurrection from the dead'. Galatians 4:4 makes it a sending, into time and under law. Hebrews 1:5 makes it a quotation of Psalm 2:7 and 2 Samuel 7:14, applied to no angel.

Romans 8:32 is the one that reaches back: 'He who did not spare His own Son' is the language of Genesis 22:12, 'you have not withheld your only son', said to Abraham. Paul does not mention Abraham in the verse, and the text records the wording rather than the claim.

items.label: is drawn on by
items.name: He who did not spare His own Son

the_son_of_man.name: the Son of Man
the_son_of_man.desc:
**Seventy-six verses, and seventy-four are in the gospels.** It is the title the narrative uses and the letters do not: two occurrences outside Matthew, Mark, Luke, John and Acts in the whole New Testament.

It is also the one Jesus uses of himself, and almost nobody uses of him. Stephen at Acts 7:56 is the exception, and he is dying.

Its source is stated at Mark 14:62, which quotes it back at the high priest: 'you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven' -- Daniel 7:13, 'One like the Son of Man coming with the clouds of heaven'. **The answer that gets him condemned is a quotation.**

items.name: the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath

the_spear_of_saul.name: the spear of Saul
the_spear_of_saul.desc: Thrown at David twice, and then stuck in the ground at Saul's bolster while he sleeps, where David takes it instead of using it. Saul is leaning on it when he dies (2Sam 1:6).

the_spirit_of_god_moved_upon_the_face_of.name: the Spirit of God was hovering over the surface of the waters
the_spirit_of_god_moved_upon_the_face_of.desc:
'Now the earth was formless and void, and darkness was over the surface of the deep. And the Spirit of God was hovering over the surface of the waters.' (Gen 1:2).

The Spirit is present in Scripture's second sentence, before anything is made and before anything is said.

the_spirit_of_truth.name: the Spirit of truth
the_spirit_of_truth.desc:
'the Spirit of truth. The world cannot receive Him, because it neither sees Him nor knows Him.' (John 14:17).

The second title in the same discourse, and twice it is laid directly alongside the first — 'another Advocate ... the Spirit of truth' (14:16-17), 'When the Advocate comes ... the Spirit of truth' (15:26). One speaker, one evening, two names.

John 16:13 is the verse that draws a line Scripture rarely draws between the persons: 'He will not speak on His own, but He will speak what He hears'.

items.label: is drawn on by
items.name: taking from what is Mine and disclosing it to you

the_stone_the_builders_rejected.name: The stone the builders rejected
the_stone_the_builders_rejected.desc:
'The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. This is from the LORD, and it is marvelous in our eyes' (Ps 118:22-23).

The most-quoted of the stone sayings. Jesus cites it against the chief priests (Matt 21:42, Mark 12:10), Peter before the council (Acts 4:11), and 1Pet 2:7 sets it beside Isa 28:16. Matt 21:42 quotes verse 23 with it, so the marvel is part of what is repeated.
aka: The stone which the builders rejected

the_strait_gate_and_the_narrow_way.name: the narrow gate and the narrow way

the_strange_wives.name: the strange wives
the_strange_wives.desc: Foreign wives taken by men of the return and put away. The text names them only as a class and never individually.

the_stronger_people.name: the stronger people
the_stronger_people.desc: one people will be stronger than the other.

the_sufferings_of_this_present_time.name: our present sufferings
the_sufferings_of_this_present_time.desc:
'I consider that our present sufferings are not comparable to the glory that will be revealed in us.' (Rom 8:18).

**A comparison the verse declines to make**, which is the point of it: the two are said to be incommensurable rather than weighed.

items.label: is used as an image for
items.name: an eternal weight of glory that is far beyond comparison

the_sure_mercies_of_david.name: My loving devotion promised to David
the_sure_mercies_of_david.desc:
'I will make with you an everlasting covenant-My loving devotion promised to David.' (Isa 55:3).

**The mercies are David's and the covenant is with somebody else** -- Isaiah offers what was promised to one man to whoever will incline their ear. Paul reads it as fulfilled in the resurrection: 'never to see decay. As He has said: I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David.' (Acts 13:34).

items.label: is drawn on by
items.name: we proclaim to you the good news

items.name: Mercy & Restoration (major theme)

the_sword_of_goliath.name: the sword of Goliath
the_sword_of_goliath.desc: Taken off the body David had just killed with a stone, and kept at Nob wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. When David arrives unarmed and asks what weapons are there, the priest offers this one, and David answers 'There is none like it; give it to me.' Doeg reports the transaction and it is part of what gets the priests of Nob killed.
aka: the sword of Goliath the Philistine

the_synagogue.name: the synagogue
the_synagogue.desc: The synagogue Jesus enters again in Mark 3:1: "Once again Jesus entered the synagogue". The verse does not name the town.

the_tabernacle_of_david.name: tent of David
the_tabernacle_of_david.desc:
'In that day I will restore the fallen tent of David.' (Amos 9:11).

James quotes it at the Jerusalem council to settle an argument about Gentiles (Acts 15:16), which is a striking use: a promise about rebuilding a Jewish ruin, produced as the reason for not burdening non-Jews. The text records the quotation and the argument it was used in, and stops there.

the_temptation_in_the_wilderness.name: the temptation in the wilderness
the_temptation_in_the_wilderness.desc: "He was there in the wilderness forty days, tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals" -- the forty days Jesus spent in the wilderness.

the_thing_as_it_is.name: sound insight
the_thing_as_it_is.desc: the thing as it is, i.e., the truth, in Job's question

the_thing_jacob_requires.name: this one thing
the_thing_jacob_requires.desc: If you do this one thing for me

items.label: is the condition for
items.name: Jacob proposes the marked animals as his hire

the_thing_which_i_greatly_feared.name: the thing I feared
the_thing_which_i_greatly_feared.desc: The thing Job says he greatly feared, which then came upon him.

the_things_which_are_not_seen_are_eterna.name: what is unseen is eternal
the_things_which_are_not_seen_are_eterna.desc:
'So we fix our eyes not on what is seen, but on what is unseen. For what is seen is temporary, but what is unseen is eternal.' (2Cor 4:18).

**The same phrase Hebrews uses to define faith.** Heb 11:1 calls faith 'the certainty of what we do not see'; here the things not seen are given a property -- they are the lasting ones -- and the seen are the temporary ones. Two writers, one phrase, and neither cites the other.

What it is attached to matters as much. It closes an argument about affliction (v17) and comes one chapter before 'For we walk by faith, not by sight' (2Cor 5:7), which is the same contrast turned into a way of going about.

the_thirty_pieces_of_silver.name: the thirty pieces of silver
the_thirty_pieces_of_silver.desc:
'So they weighed out my wages, thirty pieces of silver. And the LORD said to me, Throw it to the potter' (Zech 11:12-13), quoted at Matt 27:9-10.

Matthew attributes it to Jeremiah. 'Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled' — and the silver, the price, and the potter are all in Zechariah, not in Jeremiah. Jeremiah has a potter (18:1-6) and a field bought for silver (32:6-9), which is as close as Scripture comes.

Held as it stands, with both books cited, because the discrepancy is in the text and the text's job is to show it rather than to pick a side. The same principle Scripture's own scribes worked by: copy what is there.

the_three_named_together.name: the three named together
the_three_named_together.desc:
The places Scripture names the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit in one breath.

'baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit' (Matt 28:19). 'The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit' (2Cor 13:14).

And 1 John 5:7: 'For there are three that testify' This is the most explicit statement of the three in Scripture and it is the one whose text is disputed. The clause is known as the Johannine Comma and is absent from the early Greek manuscripts. The following verse reads 'the Spirit, the water, and the blood'.

It is recorded here because leaving out a verse readers will look for is its own kind of claim, and it carries its textual status because a proof text without one would discredit every other citation.

the_three_wives.name: the three wives of his sons
the_three_wives.desc: The unnamed wives of Shem, Ham, and Japheth; 'and the three wives of his sons' (Gen 7:13).

the_throne_of_david.name: the throne of David
the_throne_of_david.desc:
'He will reign on the throne of David and over his kingdom, to establish and sustain it with justice and righteousness from that time and forevermore.' (Isa 9:7).

A phrase Scripture keeps using long after the throne is gone. 2 Samuel 7:16 promises it; Isaiah and Jeremiah use it while the monarchy is failing or finished; Gabriel uses it of an unborn child 'in the time of Herod king of Judea' (Luke 1:5) — 'The Lord God will give Him the throne of His father David' (Luke 1:32).

What the phrase refers to after the last king in Jerusalem is taken to Babylon (2 Kgs 25:7) is the question, and the text does not answer it.

the_tithe.desc: A tenth. Older than the law -- Abram pays it to Melchizedek in Genesis 14 and Jacob vows it at Bethel -- and Hebrews 7 argues from that priority, that Levi 'paid the tenth through Abraham' while still in his ancestor's loins.

the_treasure_hid_in_a_field.desc: He hides it again before buying the field, and the parable does not remark on that.

the_tribute_penny.name: the tribute penny
the_tribute_penny.desc: Asked for, produced by someone else, and turned into a question about whose face is on it. The coin does the argument rather than the answer does.

the_true_light.name: the true Light
the_true_light.desc:
'The true Light, who gives light to everyone, was coming into the world.' (John 1:9).

The adjective does work: a true light implies others. It is the same claim John 8:12 puts in the first person, 'I am the light of the world', and here it is made about him rather than by him.

the_true_vine.name: the true vine
the_true_vine.desc: Claimed at John 15:1, with the Father as the keeper of the vineyard.

the_trumpets_and_the_pitchers.name: the trumpets, and the pitchers, and the lamps
the_trumpets_and_the_pitchers.desc:
'The three companies blew their horns and shattered their jars. Holding the torches in their left hands' (Judg 7:20).

**Three hundred men, and no weapon in the account of the attack.** Each carries a trumpet in one hand and a lamp in the other, which leaves nothing to fight with, and the chapter has already explained why the army was reduced from thirty-two thousand: 'lest Israel glorify themselves over Me, saying, My own hand has saved me' (7:2).

the_vail_over_his_face.name: the veil over his face
the_vail_over_his_face.desc:
'We are not like Moses, who would put a veil over his face to keep the Israelites from gazing at the end of what was fading away.' (2Cor 3:13).

**Paul takes an object out of the Exodus narrative and makes it a figure for reading.** The veil moves from Moses's face to the hearers' minds within two verses -- 'to this day the same veil remains at the reading of the old covenant. It has not been lifted' (3:14) -- and then becomes something removable: 'But whenever anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away' (3:16).

*Three different things wear it in four verses*, and the passage never says it has changed the subject.

the_voice_of_one_crying_in_the_wildernes.name: A voice of one calling in the wilderness
the_voice_of_one_crying_in_the_wildernes.desc:
'A voice of one calling: Prepare the way for the LORD in the wilderness' (Isa 40:3).

**All four gospels apply it to John, and John applies it to himself.** Asked who he is, he answers with the verse and nothing else: 'I am a voice of one calling in the wilderness' (John 1:23). It is the rare case where the identification is made by the person identified.

the_wages_of_sin_is_death.name: the wages of sin is death
the_wages_of_sin_is_death.desc:
'For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.' (Rom 6:23).

**Wages against gift, and the pairing is the argument.** One is earned and the other is not, and the verse sets the two economies in the same sentence rather than arguing from one to the other.

the_wages_of_sin_is_death_but_the_gift_o.desc: Two halves that do not match on purpose: wages against gift, earned against given.

the_washing_of_regeneration.name: the washing of new birth
the_washing_of_regeneration.desc:
'He saved us, not by the righteous deeds we had done, but according to His mercy, through the washing of new birth and renewal by the Holy Spirit.' (Titus 3:5).

**Another not-X-but-Y, and the X being denied is righteousness.**

the_waters_are_peoples.name: the waters which you saw are peoples
the_waters_are_peoples.desc:
'The waters you saw, where the prostitute was seated, are peoples and multitudes and nations and tongues' (Rev 17:15).

Three keys are given in one chapter and they are the densest run of self-interpretation in the book: the seven heads are seven mountains (17:9), the waters are peoples (17:15), and the woman is that great city (17:18).

What the great city is, the chapter does not say. It gives a name written on a forehead — 'MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT' (17:5) — and stops.

the_full_armor_of_god.name: the full armor of God
the_full_armor_of_god.desc:
'Put on the full armor of God' (Eph 6:11), and six pieces follow, each named with what it stands for.

A declared list, and unusually the passage supplies its own key. Elsewhere a figure is left to the reader; here every item is glossed in the same clause that introduces it — the breastplate of righteousness, the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, 'which is the word of God' (6:17).

the_whole_creation_groans.name: the whole creation has been groaning
the_whole_creation_groans.desc:
'We know that the whole creation has been groaning together in the pains of childbirth until the present time.' (Rom 8:22).

Four verses whose subject is not people. The creature waits (v19), was subjected to futility, not by its own will (v20), and is to be delivered into 'the glorious freedom of the children of God' (v21) -- its release tied to theirs. This is the first of three groanings in the chapter: creation (v22), believers (v23), and the Spirit (v26).

the_wise_men_could_not.name: the magicians could not show the king
the_wise_men_could_not.desc:
'He sent and called for all the magicians of Egypt, and all the wise men thereof ... but there was none that could interpret them unto Pharaoh' (Gen 41:8).

The same scene happens twice, a thousand years and an empire apart, and neither text mentions the other. A foreign king is troubled by a dream; the professionals of the court are summoned and fail; a Hebrew captive is produced, disclaims the ability himself, credits God, interprets, and is promoted to rule over the province.

Daniel 2:27-28 is almost a restatement of Genesis 41:16: 'No wise man, enchanter, medium, or magician can explain to the king the mystery of which he inquires. But there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries'.

This is a shape rather than a citation. No verse joins the two episodes.

the_word_of_god_title.name: The Word of God
the_word_of_god_title.desc: 'and His name is The Word of God' (Rev 19:13); 'In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God' (John 1:1). A name given to a person, which is a different thing from what God speaks; the question of how they are related is not settled in the text.

the_word_was_made_flesh.name: The Word became flesh

'The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us. We have seen His glory, the glory of the one and only Son from the Father, full of grace and truth.' (John 1:14).

**The verse that closes the loop on v1 and v3.** The Word that was in the beginning and by whom all things were made is now made -- the same verb the making of v3 uses, turned on the maker.

v17 names him for the first time in the chapter: 'grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.' Fourteen verses of Word, light and life, and then a name.

Hananiah breaks it off him and says God will break Babylon's the same way; Jeremiah is sent back to say the wooden yoke has been replaced with one of iron. Held apart from the figure for the reason Gideon's ephod is held apart from Aaron's: this one is an object somebody made.

theophilus.name: Theophilus
theophilus.desc:
'Therefore, having carefully investigated everything from the beginning, it seemed good also to me to write an orderly account for you, most excellent Theophilus,' (Luke 1:3), and 'In my first book, O Theophilus, I wrote' (Acts 1:1).

Two verses in all of Scripture, and they are the opening lines of two of its books. Most excellent is the same form of address Paul uses to a Roman governor — 'most excellent Festus' (Acts 26:25), 'most excellent Felix' (Acts 23:26) — which is as much as the text gives about who he was.

The asymmetry is the interesting part and it runs the opposite way from the letters. Luke names his reader and never names himself. He writes 'it seemed good also to me' and 'The first book I wrote' and stops there. Paul opens thirteen letters with his own name and this writer opens two books with somebody else's.

The text names a person, twice addressed, by someone unnamed; naming Luke would be importing a tradition the text never states.

there_has_not_come_a_razor_upon_my_head.name: My hair has never been cut
there_has_not_come_a_razor_upon_my_head.desc:
'My hair has never been cut, because I have been a Nazirite to God from my mother's womb' (Judg 16:17).

The strength is attached to a vow rather than to the hair, and the vow was made for him before he was born (13:5). What the hair does is keep the vow visible.

The verse a reader usually misses is the next one about waking: 'he did not know that the LORD had departed from him' (16:20). The text puts the loss somewhere other than the haircut.

these_great_beasts_are_four_kings.name: These four great beasts are four kings
these_great_beasts_are_four_kings.desc:
'These four great beasts are four kings who will arise from the earth.' (Dan 7:17).

**Daniel asks for the interpretation inside his own vision** -- 'I approached one of those who were standing there, and I asked him the true meaning of all this' (7:16) -- which is unusual: the seer is a character who does not understand what he is seeing.

The key is given and kept general. Four beasts, four kings, and no kingdom named.

they_parted_my_garments_among_them.desc:
'They divide my garments among them and cast lots for my clothing.' (Ps 22:18), quoted at Matt 27:35.

The last of Matthew's fulfilment citations and the smallest detail any of them cover -- not a birth, a place, or a ministry, but what soldiers did with clothing. Psalm 22 opens with the words spoken from the cross at Matt 27:46.

they_shall_renew_their_strength.name: they shall renew their strength
they_shall_renew_their_strength.desc:
'those who wait upon the LORD will renew their strength; they will mount up with wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary, they will walk and not faint.' (Isa 40:31).

**The three clauses descend rather than climb** -- mount up, run, walk -- and the promise attached to each gets smaller and more ordinary. It ends at not fainting while walking.

this_is_a_faithful_saying.desc: The formula at Titus 3:8 marking what precedes it as trustworthy.

this_is_life_eternal.name: this is eternal life
this_is_life_eternal.desc:
'Now this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.' (John 17:3).

The one place the text defines the phrase, and it defines it as knowing rather than lasting. It is also a verse cited on both sides of arguments about the Son's relation to the Father, because of what it puts beside the only true God.

this_is_with_you.name: this was in Your mind
this_is_with_you.desc: Quote: 'I know that this was in Your mind'

those_that_remain_of_the_wicked.name: Those that remain of him
those_that_remain_of_the_wicked.desc: His survivors will be buried by the plague (Job 27:15)

you_anoint_my_head_with_oil.name: You anoint my head with oil
you_anoint_my_head_with_oil.desc:
'You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows.' (Ps 23:5).

The verse where the psalm changes figure. Four verses of shepherd and sheep, and then a table, a guest, and a host attending to him — in front of the enemies rather than away from them.

The anointing here is hospitality, not commission. That distinction is the whole of why this verse sits next to 1Sam 16:13 in the text and is not the same thing: both have the word and the oil, and only one has the Spirit that follows.

you_are_the_man.name: You are that man
you_are_the_man.desc:
'Then Nathan said to David, You are that man!' (2Sam 12:7).

The rebuke arrives after the verdict, and the verdict is David's own. Nathan tells a story about a rich man taking a poor man's one ewe lamb (12:3); David is 'greatly kindled' and pronounces sentence; and then four words turn the sentence round on him.

It is the clearest demonstration in Scripture of what a parable is for. The hearer is made to judge the case before he knows he is in it, and by then he cannot un-judge it.

you_are_this_head_of_gold.name: You are that head of gold
you_are_this_head_of_gold.desc:
'You are that head of gold.' (Dan 2:38).

Daniel names the head and stops; the silver, brass and iron are given successors without names, and the text does not supply the names readers have proposed for them since.

The stone is the part the passage spends most on: 'cut out without hands' (2:34), and it breaks the image rather than joining it. What it is said to be is a kingdom (2:44), and what it is not said to be is anybody.

you_bethlehem_are_not_the_least.name: you Bethlehem
you_bethlehem_are_not_the_least.desc:
'But you, Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah, for out of you will come a ruler who will be the shepherd of My people Israel.' (Matt 2:6), citing Mic 5:2.

It is put in the mouths of the chief priests and scribes, answering Herod's question about where the Christ was to be born (Matt 2:4-5). The text has the establishment locate him correctly and take no action on it.

Micah says 'who are small among the clans of Judah'; Matthew has 'are by no means least among the rulers of Judah'. The sense is inverted and the text does not remark on it.

you_shall_love_the_lord_your_god.name: you shall love the LORD your God
you_shall_love_the_lord_your_god.desc:
'And you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.' (Deut 6:5).

Quoted three times in the gospels and the list is different every time.

    Deut 6:5     heart, soul, might
    Matt 22:37   heart, soul, mind
    Mark 12:30   heart, soul, mind, strength
    Luke 10:27   heart, soul, strength, mind

Deuteronomy gives three and the last is might. Matthew gives three and the last is mind. Mark gives four. Luke gives the same four in a different order. No two agree, and none of the gospels remarks on the difference or on departing from the verse being quoted.

you_shall_love_your_neighbor_as_yourself.desc:
'love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.' (Lev 19:18).

The second of the two, and unlike the first it is quoted the same way every time -- Matt 22:39, Mark 12:31 and Luke 10:27 all give it word for word.

**Both commandments come out of the law.** Jesus answers a question about which commandment is greatest by quoting Deuteronomy and Leviticus rather than by adding anything, and Matt 22:40 says what that is for: 'All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments.'

Held as one record because both letters quote it as scripture rather than alluding to it.

though_he_was_rich_he_became_poor.name: though He was rich, yet for your sake He became poor
though_he_was_rich_he_became_poor.desc:
'For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though He was rich, yet for your sake He became poor, so that you through His poverty might become rich.' (2Cor 8:9).

The same exchange as 2Cor 5:21 with wealth in place of righteousness, and here Paul names what he is describing: he calls it grace, in the clause before the exchange itself.

though_i_have_not_charity.name: but have not love, I am nothing

**Three verses that subtract.** Tongues, prophecy, all mysteries, all knowledge, faith enough to move mountains, everything given to the poor, the body burned -- each granted in full and then cancelled by the same clause.

It sits immediately after the list of the gifts of the Spirit and before the ranking at 13:13, and it is doing the same work as both: *this one is not like the others.*

thrust_in_your_sickle_and_reap.desc: Joel: 'Swing the sickle, for the harvest is ripe.' Revelation 14:15: 'Swing Your sickle and reap, because the time has come to harvest, for the crop of the earth is ripe.' Held as one record because the second is quoting the first almost word for word.

your_kindred.desc: Jacob's relatives, to whom he is commanded to return.

your_king_comes_unto_you.name: your King comes to you
your_king_comes_unto_you.desc:
'Rejoice greatly, O Daughter of Zion! Shout in triumph, O Daughter of Jerusalem! See, your King comes to you, righteous and victorious, humble and riding on a donkey' (Zech 9:9), quoted at Matt 21:5.

Matthew drops the rejoicing and the shouting and keeps the king, the meekness and the animal. It is the citation attached to the entry into Jerusalem, and the only one in the sweep whose fulfilment the crowd is watching happen.

your_name_shall_be_called_israel.name: Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel
your_name_shall_be_called_israel.desc:
'Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with men, and you have prevailed.' (Gen 32:28).

A name given for having won a fight the text does not explain. The opponent is called a man in 32:24, and Jacob calls the place Peniel 'I have seen God face to face' (32:30). Hosea 12:4 calls the same opponent an angel.

Three descriptions of one wrestler, none of them reconciled. And the name given becomes the name of a nation, which is the largest consequence any naming in the text has.

your_rod_and_your_staff_they_comfort_me.name: your rod and your staff they comfort me
your_rod_and_your_staff_they_comfort_me.desc: The LORD's rod and staff comfort the psalmist.

your_wickedness_great.name: your wickedness great
your_wickedness_great.desc: Eliphaz's accusation against Job: 'Is not your wickedness great?'

your_word_is_a_lamp_unto_my_feet.name: Your word is a lamp to my feet
your_word_is_a_lamp_unto_my_feet.desc:
'Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.' (Ps 119:105).

A lamp reaches as far as the next step and a light shows the way ahead. Two figures in one verse, at two distances, and the same thing is both.

It belongs with the other path verses because it answers the same question differently. Prov 3:6 has him direct the path, Ps 23:3 has him lead along it, Ps 25:4 asks to be taught it — here nothing is said about being led at all. What is given is enough light to walk by.

to_be_carnally_minded_is_death.desc:
'The mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace' (Rom 8:6), and 'the mind of the flesh is hostile to God' (8:7).

**Two minds set against each other and given outcomes rather than descriptions**, which is how Romans 8 argues throughout.

to_obey_is_better_than_sacrifice.name: obedience is better than sacrifice
to_obey_is_better_than_sacrifice.desc:
'Does the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as much as in obedience to His voice? Behold, obedience is better than sacrifice, and attentiveness is better than the fat of rams.' (1Sam 15:22).

**The third of three subtractions from the same practice, by three writers who never cite each other.** Samuel ranks obedience above sacrifice, Hosea 6:6 ranks mercy above it, Psalm 51:17 replaces its content with a broken spirit. Micah 6:6-8 asks the question all three answer.

today_you_will_be_with_me_in_paradise.name: today you will be with Me in Paradise
today_you_will_be_with_me_in_paradise.desc:
'And Jesus said to him, Truly I tell you, today you will be with Me in Paradise.' (Luke 23:43).

The only time the word paradise is spoken by Jesus in Scripture, and it is said to a man being executed beside him who has asked to be remembered at some future point. The answer moves it to the same day.

It is cited in almost every argument about what happens at death, and the text never returns to it.

tree_of_knowledge.desc:
'And in the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.' (Gen 2:9).

Named in full twice, at 2:9 and 2:17. Through Genesis 3 it is ‘the tree in the middle of the garden’ (3:3) or simply ‘the tree’ (3:6, 3:11), and after that chapter it is not mentioned again, though the text returns to the tree of life at its last page.

The two are introduced in the same sentence and stand in the same place — 'in the middle of the garden' is said of the tree of life at 2:9 and of the forbidden tree by Eve at 3:3. Which tree is in the midst is a question the text creates and does not answer.

Genesis 3:22 is where they meet: having eaten of the one, the man must be kept from the other.

Its name is built from three words, [[knowledge]], [[good]] and [[evil]], and the last two come back where the tree is not named: the [[serpent]] promises ‘you will be like God, knowing good and evil’ (3:5), and after the eating the LORD God says ‘the man has become like one of Us, knowing good and evil’ (3:22). The woman saw ‘that the tree was good for food and pleasing to the eyes, and that it was desirable for obtaining wisdom’ (3:6); when they had eaten, ‘the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked’ (3:7). What more the knowledge is, readers differ.

The pair returns later without the tree: children who ‘did not know good from evil’ (Deut 1:39), a prayer for an understanding heart ‘to discern between good and evil’ (1 Kgs 3:9), and the mature, who ‘distinguish good from evil’ (Heb 5:14).

tree_of_life.name: the tree of life
tree_of_life.desc:
Eleven verses, and they fall in three places with nothing in between: Genesis, Proverbs, Revelation.

It stands in the middle of the garden (Gen 2:9), and the garden is shut with cherubim "to guard the way to the tree of life" (3:24). It reappears at the very end -- "On either side of the river stood a tree of life, bearing twelve kinds of fruit" (Rev 22:2) -- and the way is opened again: "To the one who overcomes, I will grant the right to eat from the tree of life in the Paradise of God" (Rev 2:7); "Blessed are those who wash their robes, so that they may have the right to the tree of life" (22:14). A share in it can also be taken away (22:19).

Whether the two are one tree is not stated. Revelation 2:7 places it "in the Paradise of God", and paradise (παράδεισος) is the Septuagint's word for the garden of Genesis 2 -- which is as close as the text comes.

In between, Proverbs uses it four times as a comparison and never twice for the same thing: wisdom (3:18), the fruit of the righteous (11:30), a desire fulfilled (13:12), and a soothing tongue (15:4). A figure this fixed at both ends is remarkably loose in the middle.

'If we say we have fellowship with Him yet walk in the darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth: But if we walk in the light as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another' (1John 1:6-7).

One sentence with both halves, and the verb is the same in each. What differs is where the walking happens, and what follows from it — a lie in the first case, fellowship in the second.

No writer is attached. The first letter of John names nobody — not a name, and not a self-designation like the elder of 2 and 3 John, only 'which we have heard, which we have seen with our own eyes' (1John 1:1). The traditional attribution is not in the letter, so the saying is left unattributed.

'So I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh.' (Gal 5:16), and again at v25, 'Since we live by the Spirit, let us walk in step with the Spirit'

The instruction that stands before both lists and produces them. What follows in v17 is the reason: 'the flesh craves what is contrary to the Spirit, and the Spirit what is contrary to the flesh.' Neither list is offered as a target to aim at; both are described as what grows from a way of walking.

A different rock from Exodus 17:6, where striking is what he is told to do.

'For who has known the mind of the Lord, so as to instruct Him?” But we have the mind of Christ.' (1Cor 2:16).

**A rhetorical question from Isaiah 40:13 answered in a way the original does not invite.** The question expects nobody; the reply claims something.

we_walk_by_faith_not_by_sight.name: we walk by faith, not by sight
we_walk_by_faith_not_by_sight.desc:
'For we walk by faith, not by sight' (2Cor 5:7).

Here it is not a definition or a property but a manner of going — what is done rather than what is believed.

we_were_pharaohs_bondmen_in_egypt.name: “We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt, but the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand.
we_were_pharaohs_bondmen_in_egypt.desc: The answer the father is to say unto his son (Deut 6:21).

weakness.name: weakness
weakness.desc:
'My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.' (2Cor 12:9).

Rare as a noun — seven verses — and load-bearing where it appears. The text does not treat it as a state to be escaped: strength is perfected in it (2Cor 12:9), the Spirit helps it (Rom 8:26), the weak things are chosen (1Cor 1:27), and the high priest is touched with the feeling of it (Heb 4:15).

It is the one place Paul reports being refused. He asked three times for the thorn to be removed (2Cor 12:8) and was told no, with a reason.

what_does_the_lord_require.name: what does the LORD require of you
what_does_the_lord_require.desc:
'He has shown you, O man, what is good. And what does the LORD require of you but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?' (Mic 6:8).

**A declared list of three**, and it arrives as the answer to a question about sacrifices -- the verses before it offer burnt offerings, thousands of rams, and a firstborn child.

what_god_has_cleansed.name: Do not call anything impure that God has made clean
what_god_has_cleansed.desc:
'Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.' (Acts 10:15), said three times to a sheet let down from heaven full of animals.

Peter draws the conclusion himself and it is not about food: 'God has shown me that I should not call any man impure or unclean' (10:28). The vision is about beasts and the application is about people, and the text makes the move explicitly rather than leaving it to a reader.

what_is_truth.name: what is truth?
what_is_truth.desc:
'What is truth?' Pilate asked. And having said this, he went out again' (John 18:38).

He does not wait for an answer. The verse puts the question and the leaving in one sentence, and the text does not say whether it was asked seriously.

The other thing recorded of him is a gesture: 'he took water and washed his hands before the crowd. "I am innocent of this man's blood," he said.' (Matt 27:24) — a ritual of dissociation performed by the man with the authority to stop it.

what_mean_the_testimonies.name: “What is the meaning of the decrees and statutes and ordinances that the LORD our God has commanded you?”
what_mean_the_testimonies.desc: The son's question quoted in Deut 6:20.

when_i_am_weak_then_am_i_strong.name: when I am weak, then I am strong
when_i_am_weak_then_am_i_strong.desc:
'Therefore I take pleasure in weaknesses, in injuries, in necessities, in persecutions, and in distresses, for Christ’s sake: For when I am weak, then I am strong' (2Cor 12:10).

Stated as a conclusion drawn from v9 rather than as a paradox offered for its own sake -- 'therefore'. The list before it is of circumstances, not virtues.

where_is_the_lamb.name: where is the lamb for the burnt offering
where_is_the_lamb.desc:
'The fire and the wood are here,' said Isaac, 'but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?' (Gen 22:7) — the only thing Isaac says in the whole episode, and it is a question about what is missing.

The answer given is 'God Himself will provide the lamb' (22:8), and what is actually provided six verses later is a ram (22:13). The text does not comment on the difference between the answer and the provision, and readers have made a great deal of it.
